agentskills.name: agentskills

skill.name: skill
skill.title: Agent skill defined by a SKILL.md file
skill.desc: A skill directory as the Agent Skills specification defines it. The frontmatter fields hold the values exactly as written, with no fallbacks, so a missing or malformed value can be checked: `name` is empty when the frontmatter omits it, and `errors` explains a frontmatter that cannot be read. `directory` is what the specification requires `name` to equal, `files` lists the bundled scripts, references, and assets, and `sha256` pins the definition.

skills.name: skills
skills.title: Skills found under the directory, one per SKILL.md file

agentskills.title: Agent Skills under a directory
agentskills.desc: Skills that follow the Agent Skills specification (https://agentskills.io/specification), independent of the agent that loads them. The `path` field selects the directory searched, for example `agentskills(path: "/home/alice/src/my-skills")`. Every SKILL.md below it is a skill, including skills nested in plugin directories; the files inside a skill, `.git`, and `node_modules` are not searched. Use it to validate a skills repository against the specification or to inventory the skills in a checkout.

agentskills.skill.name: agentskills.skill

allowedTools.name: allowedTools
allowedTools.title: Tools the skill is pre-approved to use
allowedTools.desc: Frontmatter `allowed-tools` field, a space-separated list such as `Bash(git add:*) Read`. Spaces inside parentheses belong to one entry, and commas also separate entries, as some agents write them. Empty when unset.

compatibility.name: compatibility
compatibility.title: Environment requirements
compatibility.desc: Frontmatter `compatibility` field, naming the products, system packages, or network access the skill needs. The specification allows at most 500 characters. Empty when unset.

content.name: content
content.title: Full content of the SKILL.md file

description.name: description
description.title: Skill description
description.desc: Frontmatter `description` field, stating what the skill does and when to use it. The specification requires 1-1024 characters. Empty when the frontmatter omits it.

directory.name: directory
directory.title: Name of the directory that contains SKILL.md

errors.name: errors
errors.title: Problems reading the frontmatter
errors.desc: Empty when the frontmatter parses and its specified fields have the right types. Otherwise one message per problem, for example a missing or unterminated frontmatter block, invalid YAML, or a `name` that is not a string.

files.name: files
files.title: Files bundled with the skill
files.desc: Every file in the skill directory other than SKILL.md, such as those under `scripts`, `references`, and `assets`.

frontmatter.name: frontmatter
frontmatter.title: All frontmatter fields as written
frontmatter.desc: Includes fields outside the specification that individual agents read, such as `argument-hint`. Null when the frontmatter cannot be read.

license.name: license
license.title: License of the skill
license.desc: Frontmatter `license` field, a license name or the path of a bundled license file. Empty when unset.

metadata.name: metadata
metadata.title: Additional properties
metadata.desc: Frontmatter `metadata` field, a map of keys the specification leaves to the author. Null when unset.

name.name: name
name.title: Skill name
name.desc: Frontmatter `name` field. The specification requires 1-64 lowercase letters, digits, and single hyphens, equal to `directory`. Empty when the frontmatter omits it.

sha256.name: sha256
sha256.title: SHA-256 hash of the SKILL.md content

agentskills.skill.title: Agent skill defined by a SKILL.md file
agentskills.skill.desc: A skill directory as the Agent Skills specification defines it. The frontmatter fields hold the values exactly as written, with no fallbacks, so a missing or malformed value can be checked: `name` is empty when the frontmatter omits it, and `errors` explains a frontmatter that cannot be read. `directory` is what the specification requires `name` to equal, `files` lists the bundled scripts, references, and assets, and `sha256` pins the definition.

ai.name: ai

model.name: model
model.title: AI Model
model.desc: Single locally cached AI model. The `name` field identifies the model and `source` indicates which tool cached it (for example `"ollama"`, `"huggingface"`, `"lmstudio"`, `"gpt4all"`, `"pytorch"`, `"keras"`, `"tfhub"`, `"jan"`, or `"chrome"`). Use `ai.models.where(source == "ollama")` to filter by source, or inspect `size` and `modifiedAt` to find the largest or most recently used models on the system.

models.name: models
models.title: All locally cached AI models across all supported sources

ai.title: AI Model Cache
ai.desc: Locally cached AI models discovered from tools such as Ollama, Hugging Face Hub, LM Studio, GPT4All, PyTorch Hub, Keras, TensorFlow Hub, and Jan, plus the Gemini Nano model Google Chrome downloads for its built-in AI features. Iterate `models` to audit which AI models are present on the system, their sizes, file formats, publishers, and licenses.

ai.model.name: ai.model

architecture.name: architecture
architecture.title: Model architecture
architecture.desc: For example LlamaForCausalLM, MistralForCausalLM, or llama.

format.name: format
format.title: Model file format (gguf, safetensors, pytorch, h5, savedmodel, mlx, onnx, keras)

name.name: name
name.title: Model name as its tool lists it
name.desc: For example "llama3:latest" or "meta-llama/Llama-2-7b-hf". Ollama models keep a namespace other than library and a registry other than Ollama's own, as in "someuser/smollm:135m" or "hf.co/bartowski/smollm2-135m-instruct-gguf:Q4_K_M".

parameterSize.name: parameterSize
parameterSize.title: Human-readable parameter count
parameterSize.desc: For example 135M, 0.5B, 7B, or 70B. Read from the model's own metadata where the source keeps it: the parameter size Ollama records for the model, or general.size_label of a GGUF file (LM Studio, GPT4All, Jan). Otherwise only a count the model name or tag states explicitly is reported, such as the 135m of smollm:135m; empty when neither states one.

quantization.name: quantization
quantization.title: Quantization method or level
quantization.desc: For example Q4_K_M, IQ4_XS, Q8_0, F16, BF16, gptq, or awq.

source.name: source
source.title: Source tool that cached this model (ollama, huggingface, lmstudio, gpt4all, pytorch, keras, tfhub, jan, chrome)

vendor.name: vendor
vendor.title: Publisher or organization that released the model (e.g., "meta-llama", "google", "mistralai")

version.name: version
version.title: Model version identifier (e.g., Ollama tag name, HuggingFace revision hash)

ai.model.title: AI Model
ai.model.desc: Single locally cached AI model. The `name` field identifies the model and `source` indicates which tool cached it (for example `"ollama"`, `"huggingface"`, `"lmstudio"`, `"gpt4all"`, `"pytorch"`, `"keras"`, `"tfhub"`, `"jan"`, or `"chrome"`). Use `ai.models.where(source == "ollama")` to filter by source, or inspect `size` and `modifiedAt` to find the largest or most recently used models on the system.

aide.name: aide

configFile.name: configFile
configFile.title: Root configuration file the settings are read from

database.name: database
database.title: Reference database the next check compares against
database.desc: Resolved from `database_in`, with the `file:` prefix stripped. Null when the setting names no readable database, which is also the state before the database is initialized for the first time.

files.name: files
files.title: Every configuration file that contributed, including resolved includes

groups.name: groups
groups.title: Attribute group definitions, as key-value pairs
groups.desc: Maps each group name to its expression exactly as written, for example `NORMAL` to `R+sha512`. Referenced from a rule's `expression` and resolved into its `attributes`.

installed.name: installed
installed.title: Whether AIDE is present on the system
installed.desc: True when an AIDE binary is found. A configuration file left behind by a removed package does not count. Use it to guard integrity-monitoring audits on hosts that ship no AIDE at all.

newDatabase.name: newDatabase
newDatabase.title: Database a fresh initialization writes, resolved from `database_out`

params.name: params
params.title: Settings from the configuration, as key-value pairs
params.desc: Keyed by the option name as written, for example `database_in`, `database_out`, `gzip_dbout`, and `report_url`. A `key = value` line whose key is not a recognized AIDE option is reported in `groups` instead.

rule.name: rule
rule.title: AIDE selection rule
rule.desc: Single selection line from the AIDE configuration: the `path` it applies to, the `attributes` compared for matching entries, the `selection` kind deciding whether the line adds or removes coverage, and the file types it is limited to as `restriction`. Macro references in the path are substituted and the configuration's escapes (`\\.` for `\.`) removed, so `path` is the expression AIDE actually matches. Lines inside an `@@if` block whose condition is false are not rules. A condition that cannot be evaluated, such as `@@if hostname` in an image scan, has both of its branches reported. Executable files reached through `@@x_include` are run, as AIDE runs them, and their output read; on a connection that cannot run commands, such as an image scan, the rules they print are missing.

rules.name: rules
rules.title: Selection rules deciding which paths are checked

version.name: version
version.title: AIDE release reported by the aide binary
version.desc: Requires command execution, so it is null on backends that expose only a filesystem, such as an image scan, and when no aide binary can be run.

aide.title: AIDE file integrity database
aide.desc: Configuration and database state of AIDE, the Advanced Intrusion Detection Environment. `params` holds the settings read from the configuration, `groups` the attribute group definitions, and `rules` the selection lines deciding which paths are watched and which attributes are compared. `database` points at the reference database the next check runs against, and its modification time is the signal worth asserting on: a reference database older than the last package transaction no longer describes the system, so a check against it cannot detect anything that changed in between. Watch for coverage removed by a negative rule, which silently drops a path from an otherwise healthy configuration.

aide.rule.name: aide.rule

attributes.name: attributes
attributes.title: Attributes compared for entries matched by this rule
attributes.desc: Group names defined in the configuration are resolved down to the attributes they stand for, and a `-` term removes what it names. The compound groups AIDE defines itself, such as `R` and `L`, are expanded the way the installed release defines them, as `aide --version` reports. When the release is unknown, for example in an image scan, such a group is reported as written and a removal that may apply to it is kept with its sign, so `R+sha512-m-c` reads `-c`, `-m`, `R`, `sha512`.

expression.name: expression
expression.title: Attribute expression exactly as written on the line (e.g. `R+sha512`)

file.name: file
file.title: File the rule is declared in

lineNumber.name: lineNumber
lineNumber.title: Line number of the rule in its source file

path.name: path
path.title: Path or path pattern the rule applies to

restriction.name: restriction
restriction.title: File types or file system the rule is limited to
restriction.desc: The restriction written between the path and the attributes, for example `f` for regular files, `d,f` for directories and regular files, or `d=vfat` for a directory on a vfat file system. Empty when the rule applies to every entry, which `0` also states explicitly.

selection.name: selection
selection.title: How the line affects coverage
selection.desc: One of `recursive` for a plain line, `equals` for a line prefixed with `=` matching the entry itself without descending into it, `negative` for a line prefixed with `!` excluding matching entries while still descending into a matching directory, or `nonRecursiveNegative` for a line prefixed with `-` (AIDE 0.19 and later) excluding a matching directory together with everything below it. An audit for excluded paths needs to match both negative kinds.

aide.rule.title: AIDE selection rule
aide.rule.desc: Single selection line from the AIDE configuration: the `path` it applies to, the `attributes` compared for matching entries, the `selection` kind deciding whether the line adds or removes coverage, and the file types it is limited to as `restriction`. Macro references in the path are substituted and the configuration's escapes (`\\.` for `\.`) removed, so `path` is the expression AIDE actually matches. Lines inside an `@@if` block whose condition is false are not rules. A condition that cannot be evaluated, such as `@@if hostname` in an image scan, has both of its branches reported. Executable files reached through `@@x_include` are run, as AIDE runs them, and their output read; on a connection that cannot run commands, such as an image scan, the rules they print are missing.

aider.name: aider

configPath.name: configPath
configPath.title: Path to the Aider configuration file

hasApiKeys.name: hasApiKeys
hasApiKeys.title: Whether the configuration file stores provider API keys
hasApiKeys.desc: True when `openai-api-key`, `anthropic-api-key`, or any `api-key` entry holds a value. The keys themselves are never returned.

model.name: model
model.title: Configured default model
model.desc: The `model` key of the configuration file, for example "anthropic/claude-sonnet-4" or "ollama/qwen2.5-coder". Empty when unset.

package.name: package
package.title: Package that installed this tool
package.desc: Resolves to the system-package-manager entry that installed the tool when one can be identified; otherwise an abstract package (origin "unknown", empty format, absent from `packages`) that records the tool's presence and, where determinable, an inferred version. Read `.installed` for the install signal, or any package field (`version`, `purl`, `vendor`) for detail.

runtime.name: runtime
runtime.title: Host the agent runs in
runtime.desc: The environment the agent runs inside: the operating system for a standalone agent, the IDE/editor for an editor plugin, or the browser for a browser extension. The runtime's `package` carries the host's software identity (version and purl where known) so its own version and vulnerabilities can be looked up like any other software. Optional, null when the host cannot be determined.

aider.title: Aider coding assistant instance
aider.desc: Aider, a command-line AI pair-programming tool, configured on the host through .aider.conf.yml in the user's home. Queryable through it are the configured model and whether the configuration file stores provider API keys, along with the package that installed the tool and the runtime it runs in. Pass configPath to target another configuration file. URL: https://aider.chat/

skills.name: skills
skills.title: Skills installed for the agent, one resource per discovered SKILL.md file

antigravity.title: Antigravity (Google) instance
antigravity.desc: Antigravity, Google's agentic development platform, installed on the target. Reports its presence and version via package, the host it runs in via runtime, and the SKILL.md definitions installed for it via skills. Skills are scanned under the configuration directory (default .gemini/antigravity in the user's home); pass configPath to target a non-default install. Auditing this resource shows whether the agent is present and what skills extend it. URL: https://antigravity.google/

allowedTools.title: Tools the skill is allowed to use
allowedTools.desc: Tool identifiers parsed from the frontmatter `allowed-tools` field (a comma-separated list), naming the capabilities the skill may invoke such as file edits, shell commands, or web access. Empty when the skill declares no restriction. The key field for reviewing what an installed skill is permitted to do.

argumentHint.name: argumentHint
argumentHint.title: Hint for expected arguments
argumentHint.desc: Usage hint from the frontmatter `argument-hint` field, shown when the skill is invoked. Empty when unset.

content.name: content
content.title: Full raw content of the SKILL.md file
content.desc: Complete Markdown body of the skill, including the YAML frontmatter and the prose instructions the agent follows. Inspect it to review exactly what an installed skill tells the agent to do.

description.name: description
description.title: Skill description
description.desc: Free-text summary from the frontmatter `description` field, stating what the skill does and when the agent should invoke it.

name.name: name
name.title: Skill name
name.desc: Name from the SKILL.md YAML frontmatter `name` field, falling back to the skill's directory name when the frontmatter omits it.

purl.name: purl
purl.title: Package URL identifying the skill's git origin

sha256.name: sha256
sha256.title: SHA-256 hash of the skill content
sha256.desc: Hex-encoded SHA-256 digest of content, for detecting drift or pinning a known-good skill definition against a baseline.

source.name: source
source.title: Filesystem path to the SKILL.md file that defines the skill

antigravity.skill.title: Antigravity skill
antigravity.skill.desc: A single SKILL.md definition discovered for the Antigravity agent. Each skill is a Markdown file with YAML frontmatter that adds instructions and tool access to the assistant; auditing them surfaces the capabilities granted.

apache2.title: Apache2 HTTP Server
apache2.desc: Apache HTTP Server daemon version as reported by the apache2/httpd binary. Use apache2.conf for the parsed configuration, including directives, loaded modules, virtual hosts, and access-control blocks.

apache2.conf.name: apache2.conf

envvars.name: envvars
envvars.title: Environment variables sourced by Apache at startup (e.g. Debian's /etc/apache2/envvars)

file.name: file

files.name: files

params.name: params

securityHeaders.name: securityHeaders

serverSignature.name: serverSignature

serverTokens.name: serverTokens

traceEnable.name: traceEnable

traceEnable.desc: On when the configuration does not set TraceEnable, which is the httpd default.

apache2.conf.title: Apache2 HTTP Server configuration

Also surfaces hardening-relevant settings such as ServerTokens, ServerSignature, TraceEnable, and response security headers. Pass `init(path: "...")` to point at a non-default config file.

allowOverride.name: allowOverride
allowOverride.title: AllowOverride directive value (which .htaccess directives are honored, e.g. "None", "All")

params.name: params

path.name: path
path.title: Location path or regex the block matches

require.name: require
require.title: Require directive values (one entry per Require line), the access-control grants for the block

certificate.name: certificate
certificate.title: X.509 certificates parsed from sslCertificateFile

redirects.title: Redirect / RedirectMatch directives within this VirtualHost (target, status, match)

serverAliases.name: serverAliases
serverAliases.title: ServerAlias names (one entry per name across one or more ServerAlias lines)

installed.name: installed
installed.title: Whether AppArmor is present on the system

process.name: process
process.title: AppArmor confined process

profile.name: profile
profile.title: AppArmor profile

apparmor.title: AppArmor mandatory access control
apparmor.desc: AppArmor status, the loaded profiles and their enforcement modes, and the processes currently under confinement. apt.name: apt

config.name: config
config.title: APT configuration
config.desc: APT's effective configuration, as APT itself resolves it: its built-in defaults merged with `/etc/apt/apt.conf` and every file in `/etc/apt/apt.conf.d/`, read from `apt-config dump`. `params` holds every option with its full name as the key (e.g. `Acquire::http::Proxy`) and the unquoted value; a list option such as `DPkg::Pre-Invoke` holds its items joined by newlines. The bool fields audit repository trust and package selection: they parse values the way APT does (`1`/`0`, `true`/`false`, `yes`/`no`, `on`/`off`) and fall back to APT's documented default when the option is not set. Reading the configuration needs `apt-config`; where it cannot run, `params` and the bool fields are an error rather than defaults.

repo.name: repo
repo.title: APT software repository
repo.desc: A single configured APT repository parsed from a sources list: its package `type` (`deb` for binary or `deb-src` for source), the `url` it fetches from, the `distribution` (suite) and `components` it pulls, and the `file` that declares it. The security-relevant fields are `trusted`, true when the entry carries `[trusted=yes]`, which disables signature verification, and `signedBy`, the keyring path pinning which key may sign the repository. `allowInsecure`, `allowWeak`, `allowDowngradeToInsecure`, `checkValidUntil` and `checkDate` are the entry's own trust options, which override the matching apt.config option for this repository; each is null when the entry does not set it. `enabled` is false for entries commented out in a one-line sources file or marked `Enabled: no` in a deb822 file.

apt.title: Advanced Package Tool (APT) configuration
apt.desc: Debian/Ubuntu package management configuration. `repos` enumerates every configured APT repository across `/etc/apt/sources.list` and the `/etc/apt/sources.list.d/` directory, parsing both the classic one-line format and the deb822 `.sources` format. Audit repository trust from there: each `apt.repo` reports whether it is marked `trusted` (signature checks bypassed) and the `signedBy` keyring that pins which key may sign it. `apt.config` holds APT's configuration.

apt.config.name: apt.config

allowDowngradeToInsecureRepositories.name: allowDowngradeToInsecureRepositories
allowDowngradeToInsecureRepositories.title: Whether a signed repository may become unsigned
allowDowngradeToInsecureRepositories.desc: Acquire::AllowDowngradeToInsecureRepositories, default false. True when the base option or its `Binary::apt-get::` or `Binary::apt::` override is true.

allowInsecureRepositories.name: allowInsecureRepositories
allowInsecureRepositories.title: Whether repositories without a valid signature can be used
allowInsecureRepositories.desc: Acquire::AllowInsecureRepositories, default false. True when the base option or the `Binary::apt-get::` or `Binary::apt::` override of it is true, since that front-end then loads unsigned repositories. apt 1.4 (Debian 9) sets the `apt-get` override by default.

allowWeakRepositories.name: allowWeakRepositories
allowWeakRepositories.title: Whether repositories signed only with weak algorithms can be used
allowWeakRepositories.desc: Acquire::AllowWeakRepositories, default false. True when the base option or its `Binary::apt-get::` or `Binary::apt::` override is true.

checkDate.name: checkDate
checkDate.title: Whether the Date of repository metadata is checked against the system clock
checkDate.desc: Acquire::Check-Date, default true. False when the base option or its `Binary::apt-get::` or `Binary::apt::` override is false.

installRecommends.name: installRecommends
installRecommends.title: Whether recommended packages are installed with a package (APT::Install-Recommends, default true)

installSuggests.name: installSuggests
installSuggests.title: Whether suggested packages are installed with a package (APT::Install-Suggests, default false)

params.name: params
params.title: Effective APT configuration, every option as a key/value string

apt.config.title: APT configuration
apt.config.desc: APT's effective configuration, as APT itself resolves it: its built-in defaults merged with `/etc/apt/apt.conf` and every file in `/etc/apt/apt.conf.d/`, read from `apt-config dump`. `params` holds every option with its full name as the key (e.g. `Acquire::http::Proxy`) and the unquoted value; a list option such as `DPkg::Pre-Invoke` holds its items joined by newlines. The bool fields audit repository trust and package selection: they parse values the way APT does (`1`/`0`, `true`/`false`, `yes`/`no`, `on`/`off`) and fall back to APT's documented default when the option is not set. Reading the configuration needs `apt-config`; where it cannot run, `params` and the bool fields are an error rather than defaults.

apt.repo.name: apt.repo

allowDowngradeToInsecure.name: allowDowngradeToInsecure
allowDowngradeToInsecure.title: Whether this repository may go from signed to unsigned
allowDowngradeToInsecure.desc: The `allow-downgrade-to-insecure` option (`Allow-Downgrade-To-Insecure` in deb822), null when the entry does not set it and apt.config.allowDowngradeToInsecureRepositories applies.

allowInsecure.name: allowInsecure
allowInsecure.title: Whether apt uses this repository when it is unsigned
allowInsecure.desc: The `allow-insecure` option (`Allow-Insecure` in deb822), null when the entry does not set it and apt.config.allowInsecureRepositories applies.

allowWeak.name: allowWeak
allowWeak.title: Whether apt uses this repository when it is signed only with weak algorithms
allowWeak.desc: The `allow-weak` option (`Allow-Weak` in deb822), null when the entry does not set it and apt.config.allowWeakRepositories applies.

checkDate.name: checkDate
checkDate.title: Whether apt rejects this repository's metadata when its Date is in the future

checkValidUntil.name: checkValidUntil

apt.repo.desc: A single configured APT repository parsed from a sources list: its package `type` (`deb` for binary or `deb-src` for source), the `url` it fetches from, the `distribution` (suite) and `components` it pulls, and the `file` that declares it. The security-relevant fields are `trusted`, true when the entry carries `[trusted=yes]`, which disables signature verification, and `signedBy`, the keyring path pinning which key may sign the repository. `allowInsecure`, `allowWeak`, `allowDowngradeToInsecure`, `checkValidUntil` and `checkDate` are the entry's own trust options, which override the matching apt.config option for this repository; each is null when the entry does not set it. `enabled` is false for entries commented out in a one-line sources file or marked `Enabled: no` in a deb822 file.

config.name: config
config.title: auditd (Linux Audit Daemon) global configuration
config.desc: /etc/audit/auditd.conf parameters as a key-value map, covering log rotation, disk-space thresholds, and failure actions. `params` keys such as max_log_file, space_left_action, and disk_full_action drive audit-logging hardening checks.

rules.name: rules
rules.title: auditd (Linux Audit Daemon) ruleset on disk
rules.desc: Kernel audit ruleset as loaded from the on-disk rule files, broken out into three families: controls (daemon and buffer settings), file watches, and syscall rules. By default the rules are read the way augenrules assembles them: the top-level *.rules files in /etc/audit/rules.d in natural sort order, falling back to /etc/audit/audit.rules when that directory has none. Pass a path to point at a different file or directory. When no rules are found the rule lists are empty and `exists` is false, so a check can tell a missing ruleset apart from one that lacks a rule. Use this to confirm that required watches (for example on /etc/shadow or /etc/sudoers) and syscall audits mandated by a hardening baseline are present.

status.name: status
status.title: auditd (Linux Audit Daemon) kernel audit status
status.desc: State of the kernel audit subsystem as reported by `auditctl -s`: whether auditing is enabled or locked, the failure mode, and backlog and loss counters. This is the loaded state, which can differ from the rules on disk. Requires running commands as root; the fields error rather than report zeros when auditctl cannot run.

actionMailAcct.name: actionMailAcct

adminSpaceLeftAction.name: adminSpaceLeftAction
adminSpaceLeftAction.title: Action taken when free disk space falls below admin_space_left (admin_space_left_action)
adminSpaceLeftAction.desc: Lowercased, for example "single" or "halt". auditd's built-in default of "ignore" when the key is absent.

diskErrorAction.name: diskErrorAction

maxLogFileAction.name: maxLogFileAction
maxLogFileAction.title: Action taken when a log file reaches max_log_file (max_log_file_action)
maxLogFileAction.desc: Lowercased, for example "rotate" or "keep_logs". auditd's built-in default of "ignore" when the key is absent.

numLogs.name: numLogs

spaceLeftAction.desc: Lowercased, for example "email" or "single". auditd's built-in default of "ignore" when the key is absent.

auditd.config.title: auditd (Linux Audit Daemon) global configuration
auditd.config.desc: /etc/audit/auditd.conf parameters as a key-value map, covering log rotation, disk-space thresholds, and failure actions. `params` keys such as max_log_file, space_left_action, and disk_full_action drive audit-logging hardening checks.

control.name: control
control.title: auditd (Linux Audit Daemon) rule for a control
control.desc: Control setting from the ruleset, split into a flag and an optional value. For example `--backlog_wait_time 60000` becomes {flag: "--backlog_wait_time", value: "60000"}, `-b 8192` becomes {flag: "-b", value: "8192"}, and a valueless `-D` (delete all rules) becomes {flag: "-D", value: nil}.

file.name: file
file.title: auditd (Linux Audit Daemon) rule for a file
file.desc: File watch rule (-w) describing a path auditd monitors, the access types that trigger an event, and the key that tags matching records. For example `-w /etc/shadow -p rw -k shadow_access` becomes {path: "/etc/shadow", permissions: "rw", keyname: "shadow_access"}.

syscall.name: syscall
syscall.title: auditd (Linux Audit Daemon) rule for a syscall
syscall.desc: Syscall audit rule (-a) that fires on the listed system calls when the field filters match. For example `-a always,exit -F arch=b32 -F auid>=1000 -F auid!=unset` becomes => { action: "always", list: "exit", syscalls: [], field_entries: [ key="arch" op="=" value="b32" key="auid" op=">=" value="1000" key="auid" op="!=" value="unset" ], keyname: nil, }

watch.name: watch
watch.title: auditd (Linux Audit Daemon) file watch, in either syntax
watch.desc: Normalized form of a watch rule. `-w /etc/shadow -p wa -k identity` and `-a always,exit -F path=/etc/shadow -F perm=aw -k identity` both become {path: "/etc/shadow", permissions: ["w", "a"], keyname: "identity"}.

auidMin.name: auidMin
auidMin.title: Minimum audit UID this rule is restricted to
auidMin.desc: The threshold N from a `-F auid>=N` filter, commonly `1000` to target interactive users above the system UID range. Null when the rule has no `auid>=` filter.

comparisons.name: comparisons

excludesUnsetAuid.name: excludesUnsetAuid
excludesUnsetAuid.title: Whether the rule excludes events with an unset audit UID
excludesUnsetAuid.desc: True when the rule carries a `-F auid!=unset` filter (also matching the raw sentinels `4294967295` and `-1`), which drops events from daemons and other processes that never had a login UID assigned.

fields.name: fields
fields.title: Raw field filters (from -F), each entry a {key, op, value} dict

keyname.name: keyname
keyname.title: Key tagging records this rule produces (from -k or -F key=), for filtering audit logs

syscalls.name: syscalls

auditd.rule.syscall.title: auditd (Linux Audit Daemon) rule for a syscall
auditd.rule.syscall.desc: Syscall audit rule (-a) that fires on the listed system calls when the field filters match. For example `-a always,exit -F arch=b32 -F auid>=1000 -F auid!=unset` becomes => { action: "always", list: "exit", syscalls: [], field_entries: [ key="arch" op="=" value="b32" key="auid" op=">=" value="1000" key="auid" op="!=" value="unset" ], keyname: nil, }

exists.name: exists
exists.title: Whether any rule file was found at path
exists.desc: False when neither /etc/audit/rules.d holds *.rules files nor /etc/audit/audit.rules exists. Guard checks with `auditd.rules.exists && ...` on the same line to fail, rather than pass on an empty list, when no ruleset is present.

files.name: files
files.title: File watch rules (-w entries)
files.desc: A watch removed by a later matching -W rule, in the same file or a later one, is not listed.

immutable.name: immutable
immutable.title: Whether the ruleset locks the audit configuration (-e 2)
immutable.desc: For a rules directory, augenrules keeps only the last -e control, so this is true when that last one is `-e 2`. For a single rules file, auditctl applies rules in order and ignores changes after `-e 2`, so any `-e 2` makes it true. False when there is no -e control.

path.name: path
path.title: Directory or file the rules are read from
path.desc: /etc/audit/rules.d when it holds *.rules files, otherwise /etc/audit/audit.rules when that file exists, otherwise /etc/audit/rules.d.

syscalls.name: syscalls
syscalls.title: Syscall audit rules (-a and -A entries)
syscalls.desc: A rule removed by a later matching -d rule is not listed. The match is the one the kernel makes: the same list, action, syscalls, fields in order, and key.

watches.name: watches
watches.title: File watches in both syntaxes, normalized
watches.desc: Combines -w rules with the equivalent syscall form `-a always,exit -F path=... -F perm=...` (or `-F dir=`), which auditctl -l prints and several hardening guides prescribe. Paths lose any trailing slash and permissions become a set, so `-p aw` and `-p wa` compare equal. A watch removed by a later matching -W or -d rule is not listed.

auditd.rules.title: auditd (Linux Audit Daemon) ruleset on disk
auditd.rules.desc: Kernel audit ruleset as loaded from the on-disk rule files, broken out into three families: controls (daemon and buffer settings), file watches, and syscall rules. By default the rules are read the way augenrules assembles them: the top-level *.rules files in /etc/audit/rules.d in natural sort order, falling back to /etc/audit/audit.rules when that directory has none. Pass a path to point at a different file or directory. When no rules are found the rule lists are empty and `exists` is false, so a check can tell a missing ruleset apart from one that lacks a rule. Use this to confirm that required watches (for example on /etc/shadow or /etc/sudoers) and syscall audits mandated by a hardening baseline are present.

cassandra.name: cassandra

conf.name: conf
conf.title: Apache Cassandra cassandra.yaml file
conf.desc:
Settings from the main Cassandra configuration file on disk, useful for auditing the cluster's declared posture without a CQL session or credentials, and for detecting drift between the file and a running node that has not been restarted since it was edited. The file is a nested YAML document and has no include mechanism, so a parse reads exactly one file and `params` holds the whole tree as written.

Convenience fields flatten the branches that carry security posture: authentication and authorization, client and internode encryption, encryption at rest, audit and full query logging, network binding, the feature toggles that widen the query surface, and storage durability. Each reports the value the server would use, so an option left out of the file reads as the server default rather than as empty. That matters most where the default is permissive: `authenticator` and `authorizer` both default to their AllowAll variants, which authenticate nobody and authorize everybody.

Option names follow Cassandra 4.1 and later, which renamed most of cassandra.yaml. Settings that name an implementation class are read in both shapes the server accepts, a bare class name and a mapping carrying `class_name`. By default the file is located by probing the well-known paths for Debian/Ubuntu, RPM, and tarball installations; pass an explicit path with `cassandra.conf("/path/to/cassandra.yaml")`.

env.name: env
env.title: Apache Cassandra cassandra-env.sh file
env.desc:
JMX exposure and the JVM system properties the launch script sets, read from cassandra-env.sh. Cassandra keeps its JMX posture in this shell script rather than in cassandra.yaml, and it is not reported by the running server either, so this file is the only place the settings can be audited. `localJmx` is the consequential one: Cassandra ships with JMX bound to localhost, and turning that off exposes a port that can read and write cluster state, run nodetool operations, and, with full query log archiving on, execute shell commands.

The file is a script rather than a configuration file, and it ships with both a localhost-only and a remote branch of JMX settings present in the text. The `if [ "$LOCAL_JMX" = "yes" ]` conditional that selects between them is resolved, so `properties` holds only what the live branch sets and `jmxAuthenticate` reports the value that actually applies. Any other conditional in the file is treated as taken. Permissions on the files named by `jmxPasswordFile` and `jmxAccessFile` are worth checking alongside these, through the file resource. By default the script is located by probing the well-known paths for Debian/Ubuntu, RPM, and tarball installations; pass an explicit path with `cassandra.env("/path/to/cassandra-env.sh")`.

rackdc.name: rackdc
rackdc.title: Apache Cassandra cassandra-rackdc.properties file
rackdc.desc: Data center and rack this node reports to the cluster, which the rack-aware snitches read to place replicas. A wrong or default value here puts replicas that were meant to be spread across failure domains onto the same one, and it decides which links `internodeEncryption` set to dc or rack considers internal. By default the file is located by probing the well-known paths for Debian/Ubuntu, RPM, and tarball installations; pass an explicit path with `cassandra.rackdc("/path/to/cassandra-rackdc.properties")`.

version.name: version
version.title: Cassandra version (e.g., "5.0.2")
version.desc: Read by running the server binary, so it reports nothing over a transport that cannot run commands. The configuration files the other cassandra resources read are unaffected, since they come off the filesystem.

cassandra.title: Apache Cassandra Server
cassandra.desc: Cassandra server version as reported by the installed server binary. Use cassandra.conf for the parsed cassandra.yaml, covering authentication and authorization, client and internode encryption, at-rest encryption, audit logging, network binding, and the feature toggles that widen the query surface. JMX exposure lives in a shell script rather than in cassandra.yaml, so it is reached through cassandra.env, and the snitch topology through cassandra.rackdc.

conf.name: conf
conf.title: Chrony NTP daemon configuration
conf.desc: Configuration of chrony, the default NTP implementation on modern RHEL, Fedora, SUSE, and Debian/Ubuntu systems. The parsed fields expose the configuration in structured form so audits can assert on individual directives without regex over the raw text: `servers`, `pools`, and `peers` enumerate the configured time sources; `allow` and `deny` expose the NTP-server access control lists that decide which clients this host serves time to (an empty `allow` means the daemon does not answer client requests); `bindCmdAddresses` reports where the control socket listens; and `keyFile`, `makeStep`, and `rtcSync` cover the authentication key file, clock-stepping policy, and real-time-clock synchronization. Settings from files pulled in by `include`, `confdir`, and `sourcedir` directives are part of the parsed fields, the same files chronyd reads. Select an alternate file with `chrony.conf("...")`; the default resolves to `/etc/chrony.conf` (RHEL family), `/etc/chrony/chrony.conf` (Debian family), or `/usr/etc/chrony.conf` when the distribution ships its default there and `/etc/chrony.conf` does not exist (openSUSE Leap 16).

deviceOwnershipFromSecurityContext.title: Whether devices a pod mounts are owned by the pod's user and group rather than by root; containerd's default is false

disableApparmor.name: disableApparmor
disableApparmor.title: Whether AppArmor is turned off for all containers; containerd's default is false

disabledPlugins.name: disabledPlugins
disabledPlugins.title: Plugins containerd does not load (for example "io.containerd.grpc.v1.cri" for Docker's containerd)

enableUnprivilegedIcmp.name: enableUnprivilegedIcmp
enableUnprivilegedIcmp.title: Whether pods may send ICMP echo requests without a capability
enableUnprivilegedIcmp.desc: Sets net.ipv4.ping_group_range to every group in every pod. containerd 2.x defaults to true, 1.x to false. Null when no file sets it and the containerd version is unknown.

enableUnprivilegedPorts.name: enableUnprivilegedPorts
enableUnprivilegedPorts.title: Whether pods may bind ports below 1024 without a capability
enableUnprivilegedPorts.desc: Sets net.ipv4.ip_unprivileged_port_start to 0 in every pod. containerd 2.x defaults to true, 1.x to false. Null when no file sets it and the containerd version is unknown.

files.name: files
files.title: Configuration files, in the order containerd applies them
files.desc: `configFile` followed by the files its `imports` name, and the files those import, each overriding the ones before. Empty when `configFile` does not exist.

grpcAddress.name: grpcAddress
grpcAddress.title: Path of the socket containerd serves its API on; containerd's default is "/run/containerd/containerd.sock"

grpcGid.name: grpcGid
grpcGid.title: Group ID that owns the API socket; containerd's default is 0

grpcTcpAddress.name: grpcTcpAddress
grpcTcpAddress.title: TCP address containerd also serves its API on; empty when it serves the socket only

grpcUid.name: grpcUid
grpcUid.title: User ID that owns the API socket; containerd's default is 0

image.name: image
image.title: Image stored by containerd
image.desc: An image reference in a containerd namespace, with the `digest` and `mediaType` of its manifest or index, the `platforms` it is published for, and its `labels`. The configuration fields come from the image built for the host's platform: `configDigest` (the image ID Kubernetes reports), `size`, `createdAt`, `os`, `architecture`, `user` and `runsAsRoot`, `entrypoint`, `cmd`, `exposedPorts`, and the `layers`. They are null when containerd does not store that image's content, for example `containerd.images.where(runsAsRoot == false) { name user }`.

images.name: images
images.title: All images across every containerd namespace
images.desc: Kubernetes keeps its images in the `k8s.io` namespace. An image stored under several references is listed once for each, for example `containerd.images.where(namespace == "k8s.io" && runsAsRoot) { name }`.

process.name: process
process.title: Running containerd process; null when containerd is not running or the process list cannot be read

registryConfigPaths.name: registryConfigPaths
registryConfigPaths.title: Directories containerd looks up registry host configurations (`hosts.toml`) in
registryConfigPaths.desc: From the CRI `registry.config_path`, in the order they are tried. When neither it nor the deprecated `registry.mirrors` is set, containerd 2.x reads /etc/containerd/certs.d and /etc/docker/certs.d, and containerd 1.x none. Null when no file sets it and the containerd version is unknown.

registryHost.name: registryHost
registryHost.title: Registry host containerd pulls images from
registryHost.desc: A host of a registry namespace: a `[host."<url>"]` entry of the namespace's `hosts.toml`, tried in the order listed, or the namespace's `server`, tried last.

registryHosts.name: registryHosts
registryHosts.title: Registry hosts containerd pulls Kubernetes images from
registryHosts.desc: Read from the `hosts.toml` files in `registryConfigPaths` or, when no directory is configured, from the deprecated `registry.mirrors` and `registry.configs` settings.

restrictOomScoreAdj.name: restrictOomScoreAdj
restrictOomScoreAdj.title: Whether containerd caps the OOM score adjustment of containers at its own; containerd's default is false

root.name: root
root.title: Root directory of containerd's persistent data; containerd's default is "/var/lib/containerd"

runtime.name: runtime
runtime.title: containerd runtime handler
runtime.desc: A `containerd.runtimes.<name>` entry of the CRI configuration: the runtime a Kubernetes pod runs with when its RuntimeClass names this handler, or by default.

runtimes.name: runtimes
runtimes.title: Runtime handlers Kubernetes pods can run with

sandboxImage.name: sandboxImage
sandboxImage.title: Image of the pod sandbox (pause) container
sandboxImage.desc: Null when no file sets it and the containerd version is unknown, since the built-in default changes between releases.

selinuxEnabled.name: selinuxEnabled
selinuxEnabled.title: Whether containers run with SELinux labeling; containerd's default is false

snapshotter.name: snapshotter
snapshotter.title: Snapshotter that unpacks images for Kubernetes pods; containerd's default is "overlayfs"

state.name: state
state.title: Directory of containerd's transient state; containerd's default is "/run/containerd"

streamAddress.name: streamAddress
streamAddress.title: Listen address of the CRI streaming server for exec, attach and port forwarding
streamAddress.desc: containerd defaults to "127.0.0.1", so that only the kubelet on the node can reach it. Any other address exposes the server to the network.

streamPort.name: streamPort
streamPort.title: Port the CRI streaming server listens on; 0, containerd's default, picks a free port

streamTlsEnabled.name: streamTlsEnabled
streamTlsEnabled.title: Whether the CRI streaming server serves TLS; containerd's default is false

tolerateMissingHugetlbController.name: tolerateMissingHugetlbController
tolerateMissingHugetlbController.title: Whether containers start when the hugetlb cgroup controller is missing; containerd's default is true

version.name: version
version.title: containerd version (for example "2.2.0")
version.desc: Reported by the containerd binary. Null when it cannot be run, as on an image or a mounted filesystem.

containerd.title: containerd container runtime
containerd.desc: The containerd of a host or Kubernetes node (kubeadm, kind, K3s, RKE2, MicroK8s, k0s, and Docker's own containerd): its version, the configuration it runs with, and the containers it manages. The configuration is read from `configFile` and the files it imports, merged the way containerd merges them, and settings no file sets report containerd's built-in default, as each field says. Configuration fields read files only, so they also work on images and mounted filesystems. The registry audit is `containerd.registryHosts.none(skipVerify)`.

containerd.container.name: containerd.container

apparmorProfile.name: apparmorProfile
apparmorProfile.title: AppArmor profile the container runs with (for example "cri-containerd.apparmor.d"); empty when none is applied

boundingCapabilities.name: boundingCapabilities
boundingCapabilities.title: Bounding set of capabilities, the most the container's processes can gain

capabilities.name: capabilities
capabilities.title: Effective capabilities of the container's process (for example "CAP_NET_BIND_SERVICE")

cpuShares.name: cpuShares
cpuShares.title: Relative CPU weight (cgroup cpu shares), null when not set

gid.name: gid
gid.title: Group ID the container's process runs as

hostIPC.name: hostIPC
hostIPC.title: Whether the container shares the host's IPC namespace (hostIPC)

hostNetwork.name: hostNetwork
hostNetwork.title: Whether the container uses the host's network namespace
hostNetwork.desc: For a Kubernetes container, whether its pod sandbox does (hostNetwork).

hostPID.name: hostPID
hostPID.title: Whether the container shares the host's process namespace (hostPID)

memoryLimit.name: memoryLimit
memoryLimit.title: Memory limit in bytes, null when the container's memory is unlimited

mounts.name: mounts
mounts.title: Mounts of the container
mounts.desc: Every mount of its spec: the kernel filesystems (/proc, /sys, /dev), the files containerd and the kubelet add (/etc/hosts, the service account token), and the pod's volumes, including hostPath volumes. `mounts.where(hostPath == /containerd\.sock$/)` finds a container that controls containerd.

name.name: name
name.title: Container name within its Kubernetes pod (for example "kube-proxy"); empty for a container Kubernetes did not create

namespace.name: namespace
namespace.title: containerd namespace the container belongs to

nanoCpus.name: nanoCpus
nanoCpus.title: CPU quota in billionths of a CPU (for example 250000000 for 250m), null when unlimited

noNewPrivileges.name: noNewPrivileges
noNewPrivileges.title: Whether the container's processes are prevented from gaining privileges (allowPrivilegeEscalation false)

pid.name: pid
pid.title: Process ID of the container's task, 0 when the container is not running

pidsLimit.name: pidsLimit
pidsLimit.title: Maximum number of processes in the container, null when unlimited

podName.name: podName
podName.title: Name of the Kubernetes pod the container belongs to

podNamespace.name: podNamespace
podNamespace.title: Namespace of the Kubernetes pod the container belongs to

privileged.name: privileged
privileged.title: Whether the container runs privileged
privileged.desc: True when its spec has what privileged mode sets: /sys mounted writable and no paths of /proc masked. A privileged container keeps every capability, runs without seccomp and AppArmor, and can reach the host's devices. Null when containerd reports no spec for the container.

readOnlyRootfs.name: readOnlyRootfs
readOnlyRootfs.title: Whether the container's root filesystem is read-only

sandboxId.name: sandboxId
sandboxId.title: ID of the pod sandbox the container runs in; empty for a container Kubernetes did not create

seccompDefaultAction.name: seccompDefaultAction
seccompDefaultAction.title: Action the seccomp profile takes on system calls it does not list (for example "SCMP_ACT_ERRNO"); empty without a profile

seccompUnconfined.name: seccompUnconfined
seccompUnconfined.title: Whether no system call is filtered
seccompUnconfined.desc: True when the spec sets no seccomp profile, which is what Kubernetes's Unconfined profile and privileged mode do, or one that lets every system call run.

selinuxLabel.name: selinuxLabel
selinuxLabel.title: SELinux label of the container's process; empty when none is applied

sourceImage.name: sourceImage
sourceImage.title: Image the container was created from
sourceImage.desc: The image of `image` in the container's namespace. Null when it is no longer stored.

status.name: status
status.title: Container status (created, running, paused, stopped, unknown)

uid.name: uid
uid.title: User ID the container's process runs as, 0 for root

containerd.container.title: Single containerd container
containerd.container.desc: A container managed by containerd, identified by `id` within its `namespace`, with its `image` reference, lifecycle `status`, process `pid`, `labels`, the `runtime` handling it (e.g. `io.containerd.runc.v2`), and the `snapshotter` providing its filesystem. The confinement fields are read from the OCI runtime spec the container was created with: capabilities, seccomp, AppArmor, the host namespaces it shares, its mounts and resource limits. For a Kubernetes container they also name its pod, for example `containerd.containers.where(privileged) { podNamespace podName name }`. The pod sandbox (pause) containers are listed too.

hostPath.name: hostPath
hostPath.title: Path on the host that is mounted; empty for a mount that is not a bind mount

propagation.name: propagation
propagation.title: Mount propagation (for example "rprivate", "rslave", "rshared"); empty when not set

type.name: type
type.title: Mount type (for example "bind", "proc", "tmpfs")

containerd.image.name: containerd.image

architecture.name: architecture
architecture.title: Processor architecture the image targets (for example "amd64", "arm64")

cmd.name: cmd
cmd.title: Default arguments to `entrypoint`, or the command when there is no entrypoint

configDigest.name: configDigest
configDigest.title: Digest of the image configuration, which is the image ID Kubernetes and crictl report

containers.name: containers
containers.title: Containers created from the image, running or stopped

createdAt.name: createdAt
createdAt.title: Time the image was built, null when the image does not record it

digest.name: digest
digest.title: Digest of the image's manifest or, for a multi-platform image, its index

entrypoint.name: entrypoint
entrypoint.title: Command the image runs, prefixed to `cmd`

exposedPorts.name: exposedPorts
exposedPorts.title: Ports the image declares with `EXPOSE`, as `port/protocol` (for example "53/udp")

layers.name: layers
layers.title: Digests of the image's filesystem layers, base layer first
layers.desc: The digests of the uncompressed layer contents (diff IDs), the same whichever registry or compression the image came from.

mediaType.name: mediaType
mediaType.title: Media type of the manifest or index (for example "application/vnd.oci.image.index.v1+json")

namespace.name: namespace
namespace.title: containerd namespace the image belongs to (for example "k8s.io")

os.name: os
os.title: Operating system the image targets (for example "linux")

platforms.name: platforms
platforms.title: Platforms the image is published for (for example "linux/amd64", "linux/arm64/v8")

runsAsRoot.name: runsAsRoot
runsAsRoot.title: Whether a container started from the image runs as root
runsAsRoot.desc: True when `user` is empty, or its user part is `root` or a number equal to 0 (such as `0` or `00`). A name other than `root` counts as not root, even when the image's /etc/passwd gives it UID 0.

size.name: size
size.title: Size in bytes of the image's configuration and compressed layers

user.name: user
user.title: Account a container started from the image runs as, empty when it runs as root
user.desc: The image's `USER`, for example `65535:65535` or `nonroot`. Kubernetes overrides it with the pod's `runAsUser`, which `containerd.container.uid` reports.

variant.name: variant
variant.title: Processor architecture variant (for example "v7", "v8"); empty when the image sets none

workingDir.name: workingDir
workingDir.title: Working directory of the image's command, empty when the image sets none

containerd.image.title: Image stored by containerd
containerd.image.desc: An image reference in a containerd namespace, with the `digest` and `mediaType` of its manifest or index, the `platforms` it is published for, and its `labels`. The configuration fields come from the image built for the host's platform: `configDigest` (the image ID Kubernetes reports), `size`, `createdAt`, `os`, `architecture`, `user` and `runsAsRoot`, `entrypoint`, `cmd`, `exposedPorts`, and the `layers`. They are null when containerd does not store that image's content, for example `containerd.images.where(runsAsRoot == false) { name user }`.

containerd.registryHost.name: containerd.registryHost

caCerts.name: caCerts
caCerts.title: CA certificate files the host's certificate is verified against

capabilities.name: capabilities
capabilities.title: Operations the host is trusted with: pull, resolve (tag to digest), push
capabilities.desc: Every operation when the configuration names none.

clientCerts.name: clientCerts
clientCerts.title: Client certificate files presented to the host

file.name: file
file.title: Configuration file the host is read from; null for a host from the deprecated `registry.mirrors` or `registry.configs`

namespace.name: namespace
namespace.title: Registry namespace the host serves (for example "docker.io", or "_default" for every registry without its own)

server.name: server
server.title: Whether this is the namespace's server rather than one of its hosts (mirrors)

skipVerify.name: skipVerify
skipVerify.title: Whether the host's TLS certificate and host name go unverified

url.name: url
url.title: URL of the host (for example "https://registry-1.docker.io")
url.desc: A namespace whose hosts.toml names no server is served by its own registry. Empty for the server of the `_default` namespace without one, which is the registry each image names.

containerd.registryHost.title: Registry host containerd pulls images from
containerd.registryHost.desc: A host of a registry namespace: a `[host."<url>"]` entry of the namespace's `hosts.toml`, tried in the order listed, or the namespace's `server`, tried last.

containerd.runtime.name: containerd.runtime

baseRuntimeSpec.name: baseRuntimeSpec
baseRuntimeSpec.title: OCI runtime spec file containers start from; empty is containerd's built-in spec

isDefault.name: isDefault
isDefault.title: Whether this is the handler containers use when they ask for none

name.name: name
name.title: Handler name, as a RuntimeClass names it (for example "runc")

path.name: path
path.title: Path or name of the OCI runtime binary the shim runs; empty is runc on the PATH

podAnnotations.name: podAnnotations
podAnnotations.title: Pod annotations passed on to the runtime
podAnnotations.desc: Each one lets a pod change how the runtime runs it, for example "io.katacontainers.*".

privilegedWithoutHostDevices.name: privilegedWithoutHostDevices
privilegedWithoutHostDevices.title: Whether privileged containers run without the host's devices

root.name: root
root.title: Root directory the OCI runtime keeps container state in; empty is the runtime's default

shimPath.name: shimPath
shimPath.title: Path of the shim binary; empty when containerd finds it from `type`

systemdCgroup.name: systemdCgroup
systemdCgroup.title: Whether containers run in systemd-managed cgroups

type.name: type
type.title: Runtime type, the containerd shim that runs containers (for example "io.containerd.runc.v2")

containerd.runtime.title: containerd runtime handler
containerd.runtime.desc: A `containerd.runtimes.<name>` entry of the CRI configuration: the runtime a Kubernetes pod runs with when its RuntimeClass names this handler, or by default.

conf.name: conf
conf.title: Container engine configuration (containers.conf)
conf.desc: The containers.conf(5) configuration Podman, Buildah and Skopeo read as root, merged from the system file and its drop-ins the way Podman does. Podman 6 and later read the first of /etc/containers/containers.conf and /usr/share/containers/containers.conf, then the drop-ins in /etc/containers/containers.rootful.conf.d, /etc/containers/containers.conf.d, /usr/share/containers/containers.rootful.conf.d and /usr/share/containers/containers.conf.d in name order. Earlier versions read /usr/share/containers/containers.conf, then /etc/containers/containers.conf on top of it, then the drop-ins in /etc/containers/containers.conf.d. The version is taken from the installed podman package. Each field reports the setting containers get by default: `privileged`, `defaultCapabilities`, `seccompProfile`, and the namespace modes (`userns`, `netns`, `pidns`, `ipcns`, `utsns`, `cgroupns`) describe how much of the host a container shares unless it asks otherwise, for example `containers.conf { privileged == false && pidns != "host" }`. A setting no file sets reports the engine's default, or null where that default depends on the host, as each field says.

policy.name: policy
policy.title: Container image signature policy
policy.desc: A containers-policy.json(5) file, by default /etc/containers/policy.json, or /usr/share/containers/policy.json when that one does not exist, which is where containers-common 6 and later ship it: the requirements images must meet before Podman, Buildah, Skopeo or CRI-O pull them, by default (`defaultRequirements`) and per registry or repository (`scopes`). A requirement of type insecureAcceptAnything pulls images without verifying any signature. The `path` field selects another policy file, for example `containers.policy(path: "/etc/crio/policies/payments.json")`.

registries.name: registries
registries.title: Container image registries configuration
registries.desc: The containers-registries.conf(5) configuration that Podman, Buildah, Skopeo and CRI-O read: /etc/containers/registries.conf, or /usr/share/containers/registries.conf when it is absent, and the drop-ins in the registries.conf.d directories, merged in name order as these tools merge them for root. Each entry is the configuration for one registry or repository prefix: `containers.registries.where(insecure)` lists the ones pulled from without TLS verification, and `blocked` marks the ones pulls are refused from. `unqualifiedSearchRegistries` lists where a short image name is looked up, `shortNameMode` how a short name found in several of them is resolved, and `aliases` the short names mapped to fully qualified images.

registry.name: registry
registry.title: Configuration for one container image registry or repository prefix

storage.name: storage
storage.title: Container storage configuration (storage.conf)
storage.desc: The containers-storage.conf(5) configuration Podman, Buildah, Skopeo and CRI-O store images and containers with: /etc/containers/storage.conf, or /usr/share/containers/storage.conf when it is absent, then the drop-ins in /etc/containers/storage.rootful.conf.d, /etc/containers/storage.conf.d, /usr/share/containers/storage.rootful.conf.d and /usr/share/containers/storage.conf.d in name order, which Podman 6 and later read. `driver`, `graphRoot` and `runRoot` say where and how images and containers are stored, and `overlayMountOptions` the options overlay layers are mounted with, for example `containers.storage.overlayMountOptions.contains("nodev")`. A setting no file sets reports the library's default, or null where that default depends on the host, as each field says.

containers.conf.name: containers.conf

apparmorProfile.name: apparmorProfile
apparmorProfile.title: AppArmor profile containers run with
apparmorProfile.desc: Null when unset: the engine then applies its built-in profile, named `containers-default-` followed by the library version, on hosts that use AppArmor.

cgroupManager.name: cgroupManager
cgroupManager.title: Cgroup manager: systemd or cgroupfs
cgroupManager.desc: Null when unset: the engine then uses systemd on hosts booted with systemd and cgroupfs otherwise.

cgroupns.name: cgroupns
cgroupns.title: Cgroup namespace mode: private or host
cgroupns.desc: When unset, `private` for Podman 6 and later. Null when unset for earlier versions, which use `private` on cgroup v2 hosts and `host` on cgroup v1.

cgroups.name: cgroups
cgroups.title: Whether containers get cgroups: enabled, disabled, or no-conmon; `enabled` when unset

defaultCapabilities.name: defaultCapabilities
defaultCapabilities.title: Capabilities every container gets
defaultCapabilities.desc: When unset, the engine's default: CAP_CHOWN, CAP_DAC_OVERRIDE, CAP_FOWNER, CAP_FSETID, CAP_KILL, CAP_NET_BIND_SERVICE, CAP_SETFCAP, CAP_SETGID, CAP_SETPCAP, CAP_SETUID, and CAP_SYS_CHROOT. In upper case with the CAP_ prefix, the form the engine applies, however the files spell them.

defaultNetwork.name: defaultNetwork
defaultNetwork.title: Network containers join in bridge mode; `podman` when unset

defaultSysctls.name: defaultSysctls
defaultSysctls.title: Sysctls set in every container, as name=value (e.g., net.ipv4.ping_group_range=0 0)

defaultUlimits.name: defaultUlimits
defaultUlimits.title: Resource limits set in every container, as name=soft:hard (e.g., nofile=1024:2048)

devices.name: devices
devices.title: Host devices added to every container, as host-path:container-path:permissions

envHost.name: envHost
envHost.title: Whether every host environment variable is passed into containers; false when unset

eventsLogger.name: eventsLogger
eventsLogger.title: Where engine events are logged: journald, file, or none
eventsLogger.desc: Null when unset: the engine then uses journald on systemd hosts with a journal and file otherwise.

files.name: files
files.title: Configuration files, in the order they are applied

ipcns.name: ipcns
ipcns.title: IPC namespace mode: shareable, private, host, or none; `shareable` when unset

label.name: label
label.title: Whether containers are separated with SELinux labels
label.desc: Null when unset: the engine then labels containers whenever SELinux is enabled on the host. Ignored on hosts without SELinux.

logDriver.name: logDriver
logDriver.title: Log driver for container output: k8s-file, journald, none, or passthrough
logDriver.desc: Null when unset: the engine then uses journald when the systemd journal is available and k8s-file otherwise.

netns.name: netns
netns.title: Network namespace mode (e.g., private, bridge, host, none, pasta); `private` when unset

networkBackend.name: networkBackend
networkBackend.title: Network backend: netavark or cni
networkBackend.desc: Null when unset: Podman 6 and later use netavark, earlier versions pick cni only when it was used before.

pidns.name: pidns
pidns.title: PID namespace mode: private or host; `private` when unset

pidsLimit.name: pidsLimit
pidsLimit.title: Maximum number of processes in a container, 0 for no limit; 2048 when unset

privileged.name: privileged
privileged.title: Whether containers run privileged by default
privileged.desc: A privileged container keeps every capability and turns off the seccomp, AppArmor, SELinux and device restrictions. False when unset.

readOnly.name: readOnly
readOnly.title: Whether containers run with a read-only root filesystem; false when unset

runtime.name: runtime
runtime.title: Default OCI runtime (e.g., crun, runc, kata)
runtime.desc: Null when unset: the engine then uses the first one installed of crun, runc, runj, kata, runsc, and ocijail.

seccompProfile.name: seccompProfile
seccompProfile.title: Seccomp profile containers run with, a file path or `unconfined`
seccompProfile.desc: Null when unset: the engine then applies its default profile, /etc/containers/seccomp.json when it exists, otherwise /usr/share/containers/seccomp.json.

userns.name: userns
userns.title: User namespace mode: host, private, auto, keep-id, or nomap
userns.desc: `host` when unset, where root in the container is root on the host.

utsns.name: utsns
utsns.title: UTS namespace mode: private or host; `private` when unset

volumes.name: volumes
volumes.title: Volumes added to every container, as host-path:container-path:options

containers.conf.title: Container engine configuration (containers.conf)
containers.conf.desc: The containers.conf(5) configuration Podman, Buildah and Skopeo read as root, merged from the system file and its drop-ins the way Podman does. Podman 6 and later read the first of /etc/containers/containers.conf and /usr/share/containers/containers.conf, then the drop-ins in /etc/containers/containers.rootful.conf.d, /etc/containers/containers.conf.d, /usr/share/containers/containers.rootful.conf.d and /usr/share/containers/containers.conf.d in name order. Earlier versions read /usr/share/containers/containers.conf, then /etc/containers/containers.conf on top of it, then the drop-ins in /etc/containers/containers.conf.d. The version is taken from the installed podman package. Each field reports the setting containers get by default: `privileged`, `defaultCapabilities`, `seccompProfile`, and the namespace modes (`userns`, `netns`, `pidns`, `ipcns`, `utsns`, `cgroupns`) describe how much of the host a container shares unless it asks otherwise, for example `containers.conf { privileged == false && pidns != "host" }`. A setting no file sets reports the engine's default, or null where that default depends on the host, as each field says.

defaultRequirements.name: defaultRequirements
defaultRequirements.title: Requirements for images no scope matches

file.name: file
file.title: Policy file

requirement.name: requirement
requirement.title: Requirement of a container image signature policy

scope.name: scope
scope.title: Registry or repository of a container image signature policy with requirements of its own

scopes.name: scopes
scopes.title: Registries and repositories with requirements of their own

containers.policy.title: Container image signature policy
containers.policy.desc: A containers-policy.json(5) file, by default /etc/containers/policy.json, or /usr/share/containers/policy.json when that one does not exist, which is where containers-common 6 and later ship it: the requirements images must meet before Podman, Buildah, Skopeo or CRI-O pull them, by default (`defaultRequirements`) and per registry or repository (`scopes`). A requirement of type insecureAcceptAnything pulls images without verifying any signature. The `path` field selects another policy file, for example `containers.policy(path: "/etc/crio/policies/payments.json")`.

fulcioCAPath.name: fulcioCAPath
fulcioCAPath.title: Certificate authority that issues Fulcio certificates for keyless sigstore signatures

configuration.name: configuration
configuration.title: Effective CRI-O configuration
configuration.desc: The configuration the running CRI-O reports, with its defaults filled in. Without a running CRI-O, merged from `configFiles`, which holds only what they set.

container.name: container
container.title: CRI-O container
container.desc: A container CRI-O runs for a Kubernetes pod, with its pod (`podName`, `podNamespace`, `sandboxId`), its image, and how it is confined: read from the OCI runtime spec CRI-O created it with (its capabilities, seccomp, AppArmor and SELinux settings, user, and resource limits) and from its pod sandbox (the host namespaces it shares). The spec is stored on the node, so these fields also work when CRI-O is stopped and on a scanned image or filesystem. For example `crio.containers.where(privileged || hostPID) { podNamespace podName name }`.

containers.name: containers
containers.title: Containers CRI-O runs, without the pod sandboxes that hold them

defaultCapabilities.name: defaultCapabilities
defaultCapabilities.title: Capabilities every container gets by default (for example "CAP_CHOWN")
defaultCapabilities.desc: In upper case with the CAP_ prefix, however the configuration spells them.

defaultRuntime.name: defaultRuntime
defaultRuntime.title: Runtime handler containers use unless they ask for another (for example "crun" or "runc")

defaultSysctls.name: defaultSysctls
defaultSysctls.title: Sysctls set in every pod (for example "net.ipv4.ip_unprivileged_port_start=0")

image.name: image
image.title: Image stored by CRI-O

They are null when the image's configuration is not stored. `containers` lists the containers created from it, for example `crio.images.where(runsAsRoot && containers.length > 0) { names }`.

images.name: images

namespaceSignaturePolicy.name: namespaceSignaturePolicy
namespaceSignaturePolicy.title: Signature policy CRI-O applies to the pods of one Kubernetes namespace

readOnly.name: readOnly
readOnly.title: Whether containers run with a read-only root filesystem by default

runtime.name: runtime
runtime.title: CRI-O runtime handler
runtime.desc: A `[crio.runtime.runtimes.<name>]` entry: the low-level runtime CRI-O runs a container with when a pod's RuntimeClass names it, or by default.

runtimes.name: runtimes

seccompProfile.name: seccompProfile

streamAddress.title: Listen address of the streaming server for exec, attach and port forwarding

hostPID.name: hostPID
hostPID.title: Whether the container shares the node's process namespace (hostPID)

pidsLimit.name: pidsLimit
pidsLimit.title: Maximum number of processes in the container, null when unlimited

podName.name: podName

podNamespace.name: podNamespace
podNamespace.title: Namespace of the Kubernetes pod the container belongs to

privileged.name: privileged

readOnlyRootfs.name: readOnlyRootfs

sandboxId.name: sandboxId

uid.name: uid

selinuxRelabel.name: selinuxRelabel

architecture.name: architecture

cmd.name: cmd

createdAt.name: createdAt

entrypoint.name: entrypoint
entrypoint.title: Command the image runs, prefixed to `cmd`

exposedPorts.name: exposedPorts

repoDigests.title: Content-addressed references the image can be pulled by

workingDir.name: workingDir
workingDir.title: Working directory of the image's command, empty when the image sets none
