securityServicesRunning.title: Security services running under Virtualization-Based Security (Win32_DeviceGuard SecurityServicesRunning)
securityServicesRunning.desc: Same values as securityServicesConfigured, listing the services that are actually running rather than the ones that were asked for.

systemGuardLaunch.name: systemGuardLaunch
systemGuardLaunch.title: Whether System Guard Secure Launch is enabled (ConfigureSystemGuardLaunch)

usermodeCodeIntegrityPolicyEnforcementSt.name: usermodeCodeIntegrityPolicyEnforcementStatus
usermodeCodeIntegrityPolicyEnforcementSt.title: User-mode code integrity policy enforcement status (Win32_DeviceGuard UsermodeCodeIntegrityPolicyEnforcementStatus)

virtualizationBasedSecurityStatus.name: virtualizationBasedSecurityStatus
virtualizationBasedSecurityStatus.title: Running state of Virtualization-Based Security (Win32_DeviceGuard VirtualizationBasedSecurityStatus)
virtualizationBasedSecurityStatus.desc: 0=not enabled, 1=enabled but not running, 2=enabled and running. Where virtualizationBasedSecurityEnabled reports the policy setting, this reports whether VBS came up, so a host that is configured for VBS but lacks the platform support to run it reads 1 rather than looking compliant.

windows.deviceGuard.title: Windows Device Guard policy (Virtualization-Based Security, HVCI, and Credential Guard)
windows.deviceGuard.desc: Device Guard Group Policy values under HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies \Microsoft\Windows\DeviceGuard. These configure Virtualization-Based Security (VBS), Hypervisor-Enforced Code Integrity (HVCI / Memory Integrity), Credential Guard, System Guard Secure Launch, and kernel-mode hardware-enforced stack protection. On/off settings are exposed as booleans and graded settings (such as the HVCI and Credential Guard lock modes) as integers. Every field reads null when the underlying value is absent, so "not configured" is distinguishable from an explicit false or 0. The policy fields are read from the Windows registry, so they are available even on connections that cannot run commands. The running-state fields (`securityServicesConfigured`, `securityServicesRunning`, `availableSecurityProperties`, `codeIntegrityPolicyEnforcementStatus`, `usermodeCodeIntegrityPolicyEnforcementStatus`, and `virtualizationBasedSecurityStatus`) come from the Win32_DeviceGuard WMI class and report what the host actually negotiated at boot, which is how a service that is configured but never started becomes visible.

windows.disk.name: windows.disk

busType.name: busType
busType.title: Bus the disk is attached through
busType.desc: For example SCSI, ATA, USB, iSCSI, SAS, SATA, Virtual, File Backed Virtual, Storage Spaces, NVMe, or Unknown. Windows adds bus types over time, so a value this resource does not recognize is reported as its decimal code.

friendlyName.name: friendlyName
friendlyName.title: Display name of the disk, usually the vendor and model

healthStatus.name: healthStatus
healthStatus.title: Health status of the disk: Healthy, Warning, or Unhealthy
healthStatus.desc: A value this resource does not recognize is reported as its decimal code.

isBoot.name: isBoot
isBoot.title: Whether the disk holds the boot partition, the one with the running Windows installation

isSystem.name: isSystem
isSystem.title: Whether the disk holds the system partition, the one with the boot loader

number.name: number
number.title: Disk number the operating system assigned
number.desc: Disk 0 is typically the boot device. The number can change across restarts, so match a specific disk on `uniqueId` or `serialNumber` instead.

operationalStatus.name: operationalStatus
operationalStatus.title: Operational status of the disk
operationalStatus.desc: One entry per status Windows reports, for example "OK", "Online", "Offline", "Degraded", "Predictive Failure", "No Media", or "Failed". A status this resource does not recognize is reported as its decimal code.

partitionStyle.name: partitionStyle
partitionStyle.title: Partition style of the disk: GPT, MBR, or RAW
partitionStyle.desc: RAW is an uninitialized disk with no partition table, which Windows reports as partition style 0 (Unknown).

serialNumber.name: serialNumber
serialNumber.title: Serial number the disk reports, with surrounding whitespace removed

size.name: size
size.title: Total size of the disk in bytes

uniqueId.name: uniqueId
uniqueId.title: Disk identifier from the device identification (VPD page 0x83) data

windows.disk.title: Disk attached to a Windows computer
windows.disk.desc: A physical or virtual disk as Windows Storage Management reports it through the MSFT_Disk class. Covers identity (`number`, `friendlyName`, `serialNumber`, `uniqueId`), capacity (`size` in bytes), how the disk is attached (`busType`), how it is laid out (`partitionStyle`), whether it holds the boot or system partition, and its offline, read-only, operational, and health state. For example, `windows.disks.where(isBoot).all(size >= 64 * 1024 * 1024 * 1024)` checks the capacity of the disk Windows runs from.

windows.dnsServer.name: windows.dnsServer

diagnostics.name: diagnostics
diagnostics.title: Event log and debug log configuration

rootHint.name: rootHint
rootHint.title: Root hint name server
rootHint.desc: Single name server the resolver falls back to when it has no forwarder and no cached answer, with the addresses it is reached at. Iterated from `windows.dnsServer.rootHints`. An internal-only server is normally expected to have no root hints at all, so that a query it cannot answer fails rather than leaving the network.

rootHints.name: rootHints
rootHints.title: Root hint name servers the resolver falls back to

zone.name: zone
zone.title: DNS zone hosted by a Windows DNS Server
zone.desc:
Single zone the server is authoritative for or forwards, with the settings that decide who may transfer it, who may change it, and whether its answers are signed. Iterated from `windows.dnsServer.zones`. The `dnssec` and `signingKeys` fields are populated only for a signed zone.

A stub or forwarder zone holds no authoritative data, so the server reports no value at all for the settings that govern such data: `dynamicUpdate`, `secureSecondaries` and `notify` are empty on those zones rather than carrying one of the values listed below, and `isSigned` and `isWinsEnabled` are false because there is nothing to sign or to resolve through WINS. An audit written over the whole zone list should select the zone types it means to judge, for example `windows.dnsServer.zones.where(zoneType == "Primary")`, so that a stub zone does not fail a check about a setting it cannot have.

windows.dnsServer.title: Windows DNS Server
windows.dnsServer.desc: Configuration of the Windows DNS Server role: global server settings, recursion, resolver cache hardening, forwarders, root hints, response rate limiting, stale record scavenging, event and debug logging, and every zone the server hosts together with its zone transfer, dynamic update and DNSSEC signing configuration. Backed by the DnsServer PowerShell module, which is read once per scan in a single batched call rather than one call per field. Every field requires the DNS Server role to be installed; gate an audit on `windows.serverFeature(name: "DNS").installed` so the checks do not run on hosts that are not name servers. That gate narrows an audit but does not close it: a host where the role was added and the restart has not happened yet reports the feature as installed while the management module is still absent, and every field here reports an error on such a host rather than a configuration. Complements the client-side `dns` resource in the network provider, which resolves names through the public DNS system and cannot see a server's own configuration.

windows.dnsServer.cache.name: windows.dnsServer.cache

enablePollutionProtection.name: enablePollutionProtection
enablePollutionProtection.title: Whether the server discards records outside the queried domain

ignorePolicies.name: ignorePolicies
ignorePolicies.title: Whether the cache ignores DNS server policies

lockingPercent.name: lockingPercent
lockingPercent.title: Percentage of a record's time to live during which it cannot be overwritten
lockingPercent.desc: 100 locks a cached record for its full lifetime, which is the hardened value; a lower percentage leaves a window in which a forged response can replace it.

maxKbSize.name: maxKbSize
maxKbSize.title: Maximum cache size in kilobytes, or 0 for no limit

maxNegativeTtlSeconds.name: maxNegativeTtlSeconds
maxNegativeTtlSeconds.title: Maximum seconds a negative (name does not exist) answer is retained

maxTtlSeconds.name: maxTtlSeconds
maxTtlSeconds.title: Maximum seconds a record is retained regardless of its own time to live

storeEmptyAuthenticationResponse.name: storeEmptyAuthenticationResponse
storeEmptyAuthenticationResponse.title: Whether the server caches responses that carry no authentication data

windows.dnsServer.cache.title: Windows DNS Server resolver cache configuration
windows.dnsServer.cache.desc: Settings that govern how long the server retains resolved records and how aggressively it rejects records it did not ask for. Cache locking and pollution protection are the two settings that decide whether a cached entry can be overwritten before it expires.

windows.dnsServer.diagnostics.name: windows.dnsServer.diagnostics

enableLogFileRollover.name: enableLogFileRollover
enableLogFileRollover.title: Whether the debug log wraps rather than stopping when it reaches its size limit

enableLoggingToFile.name: enableLoggingToFile
enableLoggingToFile.title: Whether per-packet debug logging to a file is enabled

eventLogLevel.name: eventLogLevel
eventLogLevel.title: Severity of events written to the DNS Server event log
eventLogLevel.desc: 0 logs nothing, 1 logs errors, 2 logs errors and warnings, and 4 logs all events. A server that logs nothing leaves no record of a zone transfer or update failure.

filterIpAddresses.name: filterIpAddresses
filterIpAddresses.title: IP addresses the debug log is restricted to, empty when every address is logged

logAnswers.name: logAnswers
logAnswers.title: Whether outgoing answers are written to the debug log

logFilePath.name: logFilePath
logFilePath.title: Path of the debug log file, empty when the default path is used

logFullPackets.name: logFullPackets
logFullPackets.title: Whether whole packet contents are written to the debug log

logNotifications.name: logNotifications
logNotifications.title: Whether zone change notifications are written to the debug log

logQueries.name: logQueries
logQueries.title: Whether incoming queries are written to the debug log

logQuestionTransactions.name: logQuestionTransactions
logQuestionTransactions.title: Whether the question section of each packet is written to the debug log

logReceivePackets.name: logReceivePackets
logReceivePackets.title: Whether received packets are written to the debug log

logSendPackets.name: logSendPackets
logSendPackets.title: Whether sent packets are written to the debug log

logTcpPackets.name: logTcpPackets
logTcpPackets.title: Whether TCP packets are written to the debug log

logUdpPackets.name: logUdpPackets
logUdpPackets.title: Whether UDP packets are written to the debug log

logUnmatchedResponses.name: logUnmatchedResponses
logUnmatchedResponses.title: Whether responses that match no outstanding query are written to the debug log

logUpdates.name: logUpdates
logUpdates.title: Whether dynamic updates are written to the debug log

maxFileSizeBytes.name: maxFileSizeBytes
maxFileSizeBytes.title: Maximum debug log file size in bytes
maxFileSizeBytes.desc: Reported by the DnsServer module as MaxMBFileSize, but the value is a byte count and not a megabyte count: the Windows default of 500000000 is 500 MB, and it is written through to the LogFileMaxSize registry value unchanged. Compare against a size in bytes.

maxFileSizeMb.name: maxFileSizeMb
maxFileSizeMb.title: Maximum debug log file size, despite the name reported in bytes
maxFileSizeMb.desc: Deprecated in favor of maxFileSizeBytes, which carries the same value under a name that says what the unit actually is. This field is unchanged and still reports the byte count, so existing checks keep the behavior they have today. Will be removed in the next major release.

saveLogsToPersistentStorage.name: saveLogsToPersistentStorage
saveLogsToPersistentStorage.title: Whether debug log entries are flushed to disk as they are written

useSystemEventLog.name: useSystemEventLog
useSystemEventLog.title: Whether events go to the system event log rather than the DNS Server log

writeThrough.name: writeThrough
writeThrough.title: Whether each debug log entry is written through to disk immediately

windows.dnsServer.diagnostics.title: Windows DNS Server logging configuration
windows.dnsServer.diagnostics.desc: Event log severity and the per-packet debug log. The debug log records query and answer content, so it is diagnostic rather than security auditing, and leaving it on writes every query a client makes to disk.

windows.dnsServer.forwarderConfiguration.name: windows.dnsServer.forwarderConfiguration

enableReordering.name: enableReordering
enableReordering.title: Whether the server reorders forwarders by observed response time

ipAddresses.name: ipAddresses
ipAddresses.title: IP addresses queries are forwarded to, empty when no forwarders are configured

timeoutSeconds.name: timeoutSeconds
timeoutSeconds.title: Seconds the server waits for a forwarder to respond

useRootHint.name: useRootHint
useRootHint.title: Whether the server falls back to the root hints when no forwarder responds
useRootHint.desc: A server intended to forward all external traffic to controlled resolvers bypasses them entirely when this is true and the forwarders are unreachable.

windows.dnsServer.forwarderConfiguration.title: Windows DNS Server forwarder configuration
windows.dnsServer.forwarderConfiguration.desc: Servers that queries the host cannot answer itself are forwarded to, and whether the host falls back to the root hints when none of them respond.

windows.dnsServer.recursion.name: windows.dnsServer.recursion

additionalTimeoutSeconds.name: additionalTimeoutSeconds
additionalTimeoutSeconds.title: Extra seconds allowed for a recursive lookup over a slow link

enabled.name: enabled
enabled.title: Whether the server performs recursive resolution

retryIntervalSeconds.name: retryIntervalSeconds
retryIntervalSeconds.title: Seconds the server waits before retrying a recursive lookup

secureResponse.name: secureResponse
secureResponse.title: Whether the server discards responses that do not match the outstanding query
secureResponse.desc: Also known as cache pollution protection. When true the server refuses records outside the queried domain, which is what stops an off-path attacker from injecting unrelated records into the cache.

timeoutSeconds.name: timeoutSeconds
timeoutSeconds.title: Seconds the server waits for a recursive lookup to complete

windows.dnsServer.recursion.title: Windows DNS Server recursion configuration
windows.dnsServer.recursion.desc: Whether the server resolves names it is not authoritative for on behalf of clients, and the timers it applies while doing so. An authoritative server that is reachable from untrusted networks should not recurse, since an open resolver can be used to amplify reflection attacks and its cache can be poisoned.

windows.dnsServer.responseRateLimiting.name: windows.dnsServer.responseRateLimiting

errorsPerSecond.name: errorsPerSecond
errorsPerSecond.title: Identical error responses per second allowed to a client subnet

ipv4PrefixLength.name: ipv4PrefixLength
ipv4PrefixLength.title: IPv4 prefix length that defines a client subnet

ipv6PrefixLength.name: ipv6PrefixLength
ipv6PrefixLength.title: IPv6 prefix length that defines a client subnet

leakRate.name: leakRate
leakRate.title: Rate at which the server still answers one in N rate-limited queries

maximumResponsesPerWindow.name: maximumResponsesPerWindow
maximumResponsesPerWindow.title: Maximum responses allowed within a window

mode.name: mode
mode.title: Whether rate limiting is applied
mode.desc: One of Disable, Enable, or LogOnly. LogOnly records what would have been dropped without dropping it, so it does not mitigate an attack.

responsesPerSecond.name: responsesPerSecond
responsesPerSecond.title: Identical responses per second allowed to a client subnet

truncateRate.name: truncateRate
truncateRate.title: Rate at which the server returns a truncated response inviting a TCP retry

windowSeconds.name: windowSeconds
windowSeconds.title: Seconds over which responses are counted

windows.dnsServer.responseRateLimiting.title: Windows DNS Server response rate limiting configuration
windows.dnsServer.responseRateLimiting.desc: Rate limits applied to identical answers sent to the same client subnet. Without them an authoritative server can be used to amplify a reflection attack against a spoofed source address.

windows.dnsServer.rootHint.name: windows.dnsServer.rootHint

ipAddresses.name: ipAddresses
ipAddresses.title: IPv4 and IPv6 addresses the root name server is reached at

nameServer.name: nameServer
nameServer.title: Fully qualified name of the root name server

windows.dnsServer.rootHint.title: Root hint name server
windows.dnsServer.rootHint.desc: Single name server the resolver falls back to when it has no forwarder and no cached answer, with the addresses it is reached at. Iterated from `windows.dnsServer.rootHints`. An internal-only server is normally expected to have no root hints at all, so that a query it cannot answer fails rather than leaving the network.

windows.dnsServer.scavenging.name: windows.dnsServer.scavenging

enabled.name: enabled
enabled.title: Whether the server scavenges stale records

lastScavengeTime.name: lastScavengeTime
lastScavengeTime.title: Time of the last scavenging pass, null when the server has never scavenged

noRefreshIntervalSeconds.name: noRefreshIntervalSeconds
noRefreshIntervalSeconds.title: Seconds during which a record's timestamp is not refreshed

refreshIntervalSeconds.name: refreshIntervalSeconds
refreshIntervalSeconds.title: Seconds after which a record becomes eligible to be refreshed

windows.dnsServer.scavenging.title: Windows DNS Server scavenging configuration
windows.dnsServer.scavenging.desc: Automatic removal of stale dynamically registered records. Records that are never scavenged accumulate and can point a name at an address that has been reassigned to a different host.

windows.dnsServer.settings.name: windows.dnsServer.settings

addressAnswerLimit.name: addressAnswerLimit
addressAnswerLimit.title: Maximum number of address records returned in a response, or 0 for no limit

allIpAddresses.name: allIpAddresses
allIpAddresses.title: All IP addresses present on the host

bindSecondaries.name: bindSecondaries
bindSecondaries.title: Whether the server sends zone transfers to non-Microsoft secondaries in the slower, single-record format

buildNumber.name: buildNumber
buildNumber.title: Build number of the DNS server

computerName.name: computerName
computerName.title: Host name the DNS server reports for itself

dsAvailable.name: dsAvailable
dsAvailable.title: Whether Active Directory is reachable, which is required to host directory-integrated zones

enableDnsSec.name: enableDnsSec
enableDnsSec.title: Whether the server performs DNSSEC validation on responses it resolves

enableIPv6.name: enableIPv6
enableIPv6.title: Whether the server answers over IPv6

enableOnlineSigning.name: enableOnlineSigning
enableOnlineSigning.title: Whether the server signs and re-signs DNSSEC zones online without operator action

enableVersionQuery.name: enableVersionQuery
enableVersionQuery.title: Level of build information returned in response to a version query
enableVersionQuery.desc: 0 returns no version information, 1 returns the full version string, and 2 returns the version number only. A server that answers a version query discloses its exact build to an unauthenticated client, so 0 is the hardened value.

excludedPortRanges.name: excludedPortRanges
excludedPortRanges.title: Port ranges excluded from the socket pool

isReadOnlyDC.name: isReadOnlyDC
isReadOnlyDC.title: Whether the server runs on a read-only domain controller

listeningIpAddresses.name: listeningIpAddresses
listeningIpAddresses.title: IP addresses the DNS service answers on
listeningIpAddresses.desc: A server that has not been restricted to specific addresses reports every address it is bound to here, so this list is not empty on an unrestricted server and matches `allIpAddresses` instead. The restriction itself is therefore visible as this list being a subset of `allIpAddresses`, not as this list being empty.

majorVersion.name: majorVersion
majorVersion.title: Major version of the DNS server

minorVersion.name: minorVersion
minorVersion.title: Minor version of the DNS server

nameCheckFlag.name: nameCheckFlag
nameCheckFlag.title: Character set the server enforces on names
nameCheckFlag.desc: 0 allows any character, 1 enforces strict RFC 1035 names, 2 allows non-RFC ANSI names, and 3 allows multibyte UTF-8. Higher values are more permissive about what a name may contain.

rootTrustAnchorsUrl.name: rootTrustAnchorsUrl
rootTrustAnchorsUrl.title: URL the server retrieves the root trust anchors from

roundRobin.name: roundRobin
roundRobin.title: Whether the server rotates the order of multiple records in a response

serverLevelPluginDll.name: serverLevelPluginDll
serverLevelPluginDll.title: Path of a server-level plug-in DLL, empty when none is loaded
serverLevelPluginDll.desc: A plug-in DLL runs inside the DNS service and can rewrite any answer, so an unexpected value here is a server compromise indicator.

socketPoolSize.name: socketPoolSize
socketPoolSize.title: Number of sockets the server randomizes source ports across
socketPoolSize.desc: A larger pool makes the source port of an outbound query harder to guess and is the primary mitigation against cache poisoning. The Windows default is 2500 and the maximum is 10000; 0 disables randomization.

strictFileParsing.name: strictFileParsing
strictFileParsing.title: Whether the server rejects a zone file containing a bad record rather than loading it partially

xfrConnectTimeoutSeconds.name: xfrConnectTimeoutSeconds
xfrConnectTimeoutSeconds.title: Seconds the server waits for a zone transfer connection to be established

windows.dnsServer.settings.title: Windows DNS Server global settings
windows.dnsServer.settings.desc: Server-wide settings reported by Get-DnsServerSetting, covering the addresses the service answers on, the socket pool that randomizes source ports against cache poisoning, whether the server is DNSSEC aware, and whether it discloses its build in response to a version query.

windows.dnsServer.zone.name: windows.dnsServer.zone

directoryPartitionName.name: directoryPartitionName
directoryPartitionName.title: Directory partition holding a directory-integrated zone

dnssec.name: dnssec
dnssec.title: DNSSEC settings, null when the zone is not signed

dynamicUpdate.name: dynamicUpdate
dynamicUpdate.title: Which clients may register records in the zone through dynamic update
dynamicUpdate.desc: One of None, NonsecureAndSecure, or Secure, and empty on a stub or forwarder zone, which takes no dynamic updates at all. NonsecureAndSecure lets any host on the network create or overwrite a record without authenticating, so a zone that accepts it cannot be trusted to name what it claims to.

isAutoCreated.name: isAutoCreated
isAutoCreated.title: Whether the server created the zone itself rather than an operator creating it

isDsIntegrated.name: isDsIntegrated
isDsIntegrated.title: Whether the zone is stored in Active Directory rather than in a zone file

isPaused.name: isPaused
isPaused.title: Whether the zone is loaded but not answering

isReadOnly.name: isReadOnly
isReadOnly.title: Whether the zone cannot be changed on this server

isReverseLookupZone.name: isReverseLookupZone
isReverseLookupZone.title: Whether the zone maps addresses back to names

isShutdown.name: isShutdown
isShutdown.title: Whether the zone is not loaded

isSigned.name: isSigned
isSigned.title: Whether the zone is DNSSEC signed
isSigned.desc: A signed zone serves an RRSIG alongside every answer, which is what lets a validating resolver detect a forged or modified response. False on a stub or forwarder zone, which holds no records of its own to sign.

isWinsEnabled.name: isWinsEnabled
isWinsEnabled.title: Whether the zone resolves single-label names through WINS
isWinsEnabled.desc: WINS lookup embeds an unauthenticated legacy name service in the zone's answers. False on a stub or forwarder zone, which resolves nothing itself.

notify.name: notify
notify.title: Which secondaries are notified when the zone changes
notify.desc: One of NoNotify, Notify, or NotifyServers, and empty on a stub or forwarder zone, which has no secondaries to notify.

notifyServers.name: notifyServers
notifyServers.title: Servers notified when the zone changes, used when notify is NotifyServers

replicationScope.name: replicationScope
replicationScope.title: How far a directory-integrated zone replicates
replicationScope.desc: One of Forest, Domain, Legacy, or Custom, and None for a zone held in a file rather than in the directory.

secondaryServers.name: secondaryServers
secondaryServers.title: Servers explicitly allowed to transfer the zone, used when secureSecondaries is TransferToSecureServers

secureSecondaries.name: secureSecondaries
secureSecondaries.title: Which servers the zone may be transferred to
secureSecondaries.desc: One of NoTransfer, TransferAnyServer, TransferToZoneNameServer, or TransferToSecureServers, and empty on a stub or forwarder zone, which has no contents to transfer. TransferAnyServer hands the full contents of the zone, and therefore an inventory of the network, to anyone who asks.

signingKey.name: signingKey
signingKey.title: DNSSEC signing key of a zone
signingKey.desc: Single key signing key or zone signing key, described by the properties a policy can assert on: its algorithm, its length, its rollover configuration, and how long the signatures it generates stay valid. Key tags are deliberately not exposed, because they are derived from the key material and change every time the zone is re-signed, so no stable check can be written against them. Iterated from `windows.dnsServer.zone.signingKeys`.

signingKeys.name: signingKeys
signingKeys.title: DNSSEC signing keys, empty when the zone is not signed

zoneFile.name: zoneFile
zoneFile.title: Name of the zone file, empty for a directory-integrated zone

zoneType.name: zoneType
zoneType.title: Zone classification
zoneType.desc: One of Primary, Secondary, Stub, or Forwarder. Only a primary zone holds authoritative data this server can change.

windows.dnsServer.zone.title: DNS zone hosted by a Windows DNS Server
windows.dnsServer.zone.desc:
Single zone the server is authoritative for or forwards, with the settings that decide who may transfer it, who may change it, and whether its answers are signed. Iterated from `windows.dnsServer.zones`. The `dnssec` and `signingKeys` fields are populated only for a signed zone.

A stub or forwarder zone holds no authoritative data, so the server reports no value at all for the settings that govern such data: `dynamicUpdate`, `secureSecondaries` and `notify` are empty on those zones rather than carrying one of the values listed below, and `isSigned` and `isWinsEnabled` are false because there is nothing to sign or to resolve through WINS. An audit written over the whole zone list should select the zone types it means to judge, for example `windows.dnsServer.zones.where(zoneType == "Primary")`, so that a stub zone does not fail a check about a setting it cannot have.

windows.dnsServer.zone.dnssec.name: windows.dnsServer.zone.dnssec

denialOfExistence.name: denialOfExistence
denialOfExistence.title: How the zone proves a name does not exist
denialOfExistence.desc: NSec lists the next existing name in the zone, which lets anyone walk the zone and enumerate every name in it. NSec3 publishes a hash instead.

distributeTrustAnchor.name: distributeTrustAnchor
distributeTrustAnchor.title: Where the zone's trust anchor is published

dnsKeyRecordSetTtlSeconds.name: dnsKeyRecordSetTtlSeconds
dnsKeyRecordSetTtlSeconds.title: Seconds a DNSKEY record set is cached

dsRecordGenerationAlgorithm.name: dsRecordGenerationAlgorithm
dsRecordGenerationAlgorithm.title: Digest algorithms used to generate delegation signer records

dsRecordSetTtlSeconds.name: dsRecordSetTtlSeconds
dsRecordSetTtlSeconds.title: Seconds a delegation signer record set is cached

enableRfc5011KeyRollover.name: enableRfc5011KeyRollover
enableRfc5011KeyRollover.title: Whether the zone performs automated trust anchor rollover as described in RFC 5011

isKeyMasterServer.name: isKeyMasterServer
isKeyMasterServer.title: Whether this server holds the zone's signing keys

keyMasterServer.name: keyMasterServer
keyMasterServer.title: Server that holds the zone's signing keys

nsec3HashAlgorithm.name: nsec3HashAlgorithm
nsec3HashAlgorithm.title: Hash algorithm used for NSEC3 records

nsec3Iterations.name: nsec3Iterations
nsec3Iterations.title: Number of additional hash iterations applied to an NSEC3 record

nsec3OptOut.name: nsec3OptOut
nsec3OptOut.title: Whether unsigned delegations may be left unproven

nsec3RandomSaltLength.name: nsec3RandomSaltLength
nsec3RandomSaltLength.title: Length in bytes of the randomly generated NSEC3 salt

parentHasSecureDelegation.name: parentHasSecureDelegation
parentHasSecureDelegation.title: Whether the parent zone holds a delegation signer record for this zone
parentHasSecureDelegation.desc: Without it a validating resolver has no path from the parent's key to this zone's, so the signatures cannot be verified.

propagationTimeSeconds.name: propagationTimeSeconds
propagationTimeSeconds.title: Seconds allowed for a change to reach every server hosting the zone

secureDelegationPollingPeriodSeconds.name: secureDelegationPollingPeriodSeconds
secureDelegationPollingPeriodSeconds.title: Seconds between checks for an updated delegation signer record at the parent

signatureInceptionOffsetSeconds.name: signatureInceptionOffsetSeconds
signatureInceptionOffsetSeconds.title: Seconds a signature is backdated to tolerate clock skew

windows.dnsServer.zone.dnssec.title: DNSSEC settings of a signed zone
windows.dnsServer.zone.dnssec.desc: How a signed zone proves that a name does not exist, how long its generated records live, and whether it publishes a trust anchor. Present only for a zone whose `isSigned` is true.

windows.dnsServer.zone.signingKey.name: windows.dnsServer.zone.signingKey

cryptoAlgorithm.name: cryptoAlgorithm
cryptoAlgorithm.title: Signing algorithm
cryptoAlgorithm.desc: For example RsaSha1, RsaSha1NSec3, RsaSha256, RsaSha512, ECDsaP256Sha256, or ECDsaP384Sha384. The SHA-1 variants are retained for compatibility and are no longer considered collision resistant.

currentState.name: currentState
currentState.title: Lifecycle state of the key, for example Active or Standby

dnsKeySignatureValidityPeriodSeconds.name: dnsKeySignatureValidityPeriodSeconds
dnsKeySignatureValidityPeriodSeconds.title: Seconds a signature over the DNSKEY record set stays valid

dsSignatureValidityPeriodSeconds.name: dsSignatureValidityPeriodSeconds
dsSignatureValidityPeriodSeconds.title: Seconds a signature over the delegation signer record set stays valid

isRolloverEnabled.name: isRolloverEnabled
isRolloverEnabled.title: Whether the key is replaced automatically when its rollover period elapses
isRolloverEnabled.desc: A key that never rolls over stays valid indefinitely, so a compromise of its private key is permanent until an operator notices.

keyId.name: keyId
keyId.title: Identifier of the key, stable for the life of the key

keyStorageProvider.name: keyStorageProvider
keyStorageProvider.title: Cryptographic provider storing the private key

keyType.name: keyType
keyType.title: Role of the key
keyType.desc: KeySigningKey signs the zone's DNSKEY record set and is the key the parent's delegation signer record points at. ZoneSigningKey signs every other record set in the zone.

storeKeysInAD.name: storeKeysInAD
storeKeysInAD.title: Whether the private key is stored in Active Directory

zoneSignatureValidityPeriodSeconds.name: zoneSignatureValidityPeriodSeconds
zoneSignatureValidityPeriodSeconds.title: Seconds a signature over the rest of the zone stays valid
zoneSignatureValidityPeriodSeconds.desc: A long validity period widens the window in which a captured signed response can be replayed after the record behind it has changed.

windows.dnsServer.zone.signingKey.title: DNSSEC signing key of a zone
windows.dnsServer.zone.signingKey.desc: Single key signing key or zone signing key, described by the properties a policy can assert on: its algorithm, its length, its rollover configuration, and how long the signatures it generates stay valid. Key tags are deliberately not exposed, because they are derived from the key material and change every time the zone is re-signed, so no stable check can be written against them. Iterated from `windows.dnsServer.zone.signingKeys`.

windows.driver.name: windows.driver

file.name: file
file.title: Driver image on disk
file.desc: Null only when the driver records no path at all. A driver whose image was deleted still resolves here with `exists` reporting false, which is worth flagging on its own: the service entry survives the image, and a later write to that path is loaded under the driver's identity.

manufacturer.name: manufacturer
manufacturer.title: Company name recorded in the driver image

name.name: name
name.title: Service name the driver is registered under

path.name: path
path.title: Absolute path of the driver image
path.desc: Resolved from the raw registry value, which is stored in NT form such as `\??\C:\Windows\system32\drivers\foo.sys` or relative to `\SystemRoot`. Falls back to the conventional `drivers\<name>.sys` location when the registry carries no path at all.

purl.name: purl
purl.title: Package URL identifying this driver
purl.desc: A pkg:windows-driver purl whose namespace is the vendor taken from `manufacturer`, for example pkg:windows-driver/microsoft/storahci@10.0.26100.1150. Empty when the image records no company name, because a driver name alone does not identify a driver across vendors.

running.name: running
running.title: Whether the driver is currently loaded

signed.name: signed
signed.title: Whether the image carries a valid Authenticode signature
signed.desc: Null when no verdict could be reached, which is not the same as unsigned: a missing image or an unreadable certificate store leaves the question unanswered. Compare against false to find drivers measured as unsigned.

signer.name: signer
signer.title: Common name of the certificate subject that signed the image
signer.desc: For example "Microsoft Windows Hardware Compatibility Publisher". Empty when the image is unsigned or the signature could not be read.

version.name: version
version.title: File version of the driver image

windows.driver.title: Windows kernel or file system driver
windows.driver.desc: Single driver registered with the service control manager: the service `name` it loads under, the on-disk `path` of its image, the `startMode` that decides when it loads, and whether it is currently `running`. `signed` and `signer` carry the Authenticode verdict on the image, which is what a bring-your-own-vulnerable-driver audit reads, and `purl` identifies the driver for vulnerability matching in the same pkg:windows-driver namespace as windows.printerDriver.

windows.drivers.name: windows.drivers
windows.drivers.title: Kernel and file system drivers registered on the machine

windows.eventlog.name: windows.eventlog

enabled.name: enabled
enabled.title: Whether the channel is enabled and collecting events
enabled.desc: A disabled channel records nothing, so a policy that asserts a channel is large enough or retained long enough is worthless until this is true. Needs a connection that can run commands.

isClassicLog.name: isClassicLog
isClassicLog.title: Whether the channel is one of the classic pre-Vista logs
isClassicLog.desc: True for Application, Security, Setup, System and other logs kept for backward compatibility, false for a modern channel published by a provider such as Microsoft-Windows-PowerShell/Operational. Needs a connection that can run commands.

logFilePath.name: logFilePath
logFilePath.title: Full path of the channel's backing .evtx file
logFilePath.desc: For example C:\Windows\System32\Winevt\Logs\Application.evtx. Compose it with `file.acl` to check who can read or tamper with the recorded events. Needs a connection that can run commands.

maxSizeKB.name: maxSizeKB
maxSizeKB.title: Maximum log file size in KB
maxSizeKB.desc: Resolved from the first source that carries a value: the Group Policy MaxSize, the classic channel configuration under Services\EventLog, the WINEVT channel key, and then the size the channel's manifest declares. The registry holds overrides only, so a channel left at its manifest size has no value in any of those keys and only the last source knows it; that one needs a connection that can run commands, and a connection without one still resolves the registry sources. Falls back to the documented 20 MB Windows default only when no source reports a size at all.

name.name: name
name.title: Event Log channel name (for example Application, Security, Setup, or System)

overwriteAsNeeded.name: overwriteAsNeeded
overwriteAsNeeded.title: Whether the channel overwrites events as needed when full (Retention 0)

recordCount.name: recordCount
recordCount.title: Number of events currently held in the channel
recordCount.desc: Zero on a channel that has been cleared, and also on one that has never collected anything, so read it together with `enabled` rather than as evidence on its own. Needs a connection that can run commands.

retention.name: retention
retention.title: Retention behavior when the log reaches its maximum size
retention.desc: One of "overwrite_as_needed", "overwrite_by_days" (a positive retention period), or "never_overwrite". Resolved from the first source that carries a value: the Group Policy Retention, the classic channel configuration under Services\EventLog, the WINEVT channel key, and then the retention mode the channel itself reports. The first two use a period in seconds (0 as needed, a positive count of seconds by days, 4294967295 or -1 never); the WINEVT key uses a flag instead, 0 as needed and non-zero never. A modern provider channel is not under Services\EventLog at all, so without the last two sources every one of them resolved to the Windows default. Falls back to "overwrite_as_needed", the documented default, only when no source reports a behavior.

windows.eventlog.title: Windows Event Log channel configuration
windows.eventlog.desc: Size, retention policy and collection state of a single Windows Event Log channel. The `name` field selects the channel by its log name, for example `windows.eventlog(name: "Security")`, `windows.eventlog(name: "Application")` or a modern provider channel such as `windows.eventlog(name: "Microsoft-Windows-PowerShell/Operational")`. `maxSizeKB` reports the maximum log file size in KB and `retention` decodes how the channel behaves when that size is reached. `retention` reads the registry alone, so it works on a connection that cannot run commands. `enabled`, `logFilePath`, `isClassicLog` and `recordCount` report the live channel state and need a connection that can run commands.

windows.exploitProtection.name: windows.exploitProtection

available.name: available
available.title: Whether the Get-ProcessMitigation cmdlet is available on the target

cfg.name: cfg
cfg.title: Windows Exploit Protection: Control Flow Guard (CFG)
cfg.desc: CFG protects against memory-corruption exploits that hijack indirect calls. Each value is "ON", "OFF", or "NOTSET". Reached through `windows.exploitProtection.controlFlowGuard`.

disallowOverride.name: disallowOverride
disallowOverride.title: Whether users are prevented from overriding the exploit protection settings

sehop.name: sehop
sehop.title: Structured Exception Handling Overwrite Protection (SEHOP) settings

windows.exploitProtection.title: Windows Exploit Protection
windows.exploitProtection.desc: System-wide Windows Exploit Protection (the successor to EMET) configuration, reported by `Get-ProcessMitigation -System`. Five mitigations are supported system-wide: data execution prevention (`dep`), address space layout randomization (`aslr`), Control Flow Guard (`controlFlowGuard`), structured exception handling overwrite protection (`sehop`), and heap integrity (`heap`). `disallowOverride` reflects whether users may override these settings. On systems without the ProcessMitigations module the mitigation accessors resolve to null while `disallowOverride` still resolves from the registry.

windows.exploitProtection.aslr.name: windows.exploitProtection.aslr

forceRelocateImages.name: forceRelocateImages
forceRelocateImages.title: Whether images without /DYNAMICBASE are forcibly relocated

highEntropy.name: highEntropy
highEntropy.title: Whether high-entropy bottom-up randomization is enabled

requireInfo.name: requireInfo
requireInfo.title: Whether images are required to declare ASLR support

windows.exploitProtection.aslr.title: Windows Exploit Protection: address space layout randomization (ASLR)
windows.exploitProtection.aslr.desc: ASLR randomizes the memory layout of a process to frustrate exploits that rely on predictable addresses. Each value is "ON", "OFF", or "NOTSET". Reached through `windows.exploitProtection.aslr`.

windows.exploitProtection.cfg.name: windows.exploitProtection.cfg

enable.name: enable
enable.title: Whether Control Flow Guard is enabled

strictControlFlowGuard.name: strictControlFlowGuard
strictControlFlowGuard.title: Whether strict Control Flow Guard is enabled

windows.exploitProtection.cfg.title: Windows Exploit Protection: Control Flow Guard (CFG)
windows.exploitProtection.cfg.desc: CFG protects against memory-corruption exploits that hijack indirect calls. Each value is "ON", "OFF", or "NOTSET". Reached through `windows.exploitProtection.controlFlowGuard`.

windows.exploitProtection.dep.name: windows.exploitProtection.dep

emulateAtlThunks.name: emulateAtlThunks
emulateAtlThunks.title: Whether ATL thunk emulation is enabled

windows.exploitProtection.dep.title: Windows Exploit Protection: data execution prevention (DEP)
windows.exploitProtection.dep.desc: DEP prevents memory not explicitly marked executable from running as code. Each value is "ON", "OFF", or "NOTSET". Reached through `windows.exploitProtection.dep`.

windows.exploitProtection.heap.name: windows.exploitProtection.heap

terminateOnError.name: terminateOnError
terminateOnError.title: Whether the process is terminated on heap corruption

windows.exploitProtection.heap.title: Windows Exploit Protection: heap integrity
windows.exploitProtection.heap.desc: Terminating on heap corruption prevents an attacker from continuing execution after corrupting the heap. The value is "ON", "OFF", or "NOTSET". Reached through `windows.exploitProtection.heap`.

windows.exploitProtection.sehop.name: windows.exploitProtection.sehop

telemetryOnly.name: telemetryOnly
telemetryOnly.title: Whether SEHOP runs in telemetry-only mode

windows.exploitProtection.sehop.title: Windows Exploit Protection: structured exception handling overwrite protection (SEHOP)
windows.exploitProtection.sehop.desc: SEHOP blocks exploits that overwrite the structured exception handler chain. Each value is "ON", "OFF", or "NOTSET". Reached through `windows.exploitProtection.sehop`.

windows.firewall.name: windows.firewall

profile.name: profile
profile.title: Windows Firewall profile entry
profile.desc: Per-profile firewall settings for one of the three Windows Firewall profiles (Domain, Private, Public): whether the firewall is enabled, default inbound and outbound actions, local rule merge policies, unicast response behavior, stealth mode for IPsec, and log settings including max log size, allowed/blocked packet logging, and log file name.

profiles.name: profiles
profiles.title: Settings that apply to the per-profile configurations of the Windows Firewall with Advanced Security

rule.name: rule
rule.title: Windows Firewall rule entry
rule.desc: Single Windows Firewall rule: its unique `instanceID`, display name, description, group, enabled state, traffic direction (inbound/ outbound), action (allow/block), edge traversal policy, and enforcement status, together with the conditions the rule matches on: protocol, local and remote ports and addresses, ICMP types, program, service, profiles, interface types, and authorized remote principals. Iterated from `windows.firewall.rules` to audit which rules are active and what traffic they actually permit, for example an enabled inbound allow rule whose remote addresses are `Any`. The condition fields are joined onto the rule from the `Get-NetFirewallPortFilter`, `Get-NetFirewallAddressFilter`, `Get-NetFirewallApplicationFilter`, `Get-NetFirewallServiceFilter`, `Get-NetFirewallInterfaceTypeFilter`, and `Get-NetFirewallSecurityFilter` cmdlets.

rules.name: rules
rules.title: Firewall rules

settings.name: settings
settings.title: Global firewall settings (Get-NetFirewallSetting), as a dictionary of setting name to value

windows.firewall.title: Windows Firewall (Advanced Security)
windows.firewall.desc: Windows Firewall with Advanced Security posture: the global settings, the per-profile defaults (Domain, Private, Public), and every configured firewall rule. Use `profiles` to assert that the firewall is enabled and blocks inbound traffic by default on each profile, and `rules` to audit which allow/block rules are active. Backed by the `Get-NetFirewallProfile` and `Get-NetFirewallRule` PowerShell cmdlets, read from the ActiveStore: the effective policy, local configuration merged with Group Policy.

windows.firewall.profile.name: windows.firewall.profile

allowInboundRules.name: allowInboundRules
allowInboundRules.title: Whether administrators can create firewall rules that allow unsolicited inbound traffic (if 0, such rules are ignored)

allowLocalFirewallRules.name: allowLocalFirewallRules
allowLocalFirewallRules.title: Whether local firewall rules should merge into the effective policy along with group policy settings
allowLocalFirewallRules.desc: The AllowLocalPolicyMerge policy. When a policy sets it to false (0), the firewall ignores every locally defined rule, including those that `rules` lists with `policyStoreSource` PersistentStore.

allowLocalIPsecRules.name: allowLocalIPsecRules
allowLocalIPsecRules.title: Whether local IPsec rules should merge into the effective policy along with rules from group policy

allowUnicastResponseToMulticast.name: allowUnicastResponseToMulticast
allowUnicastResponseToMulticast.title: Whether to allow unicast responses to multicast traffic

allowUserApps.name: allowUserApps
allowUserApps.title: Whether to respect user allowed applications created in the legacy firewall

allowUserPorts.name: allowUserPorts
allowUserPorts.title: Whether to respect globally opened ports created in the legacy firewall

defaultInboundAction.name: defaultInboundAction
defaultInboundAction.title: Configured default action for inbound traffic
defaultInboundAction.desc: One of 0 (not configured), 2 (allow) or 4 (block). This is the action configured through policy, not the action the firewall ends up applying. A stock Windows Server install reports 0 on every profile while still blocking inbound traffic, because an unconfigured profile falls back to the firewall's own built-in default. Comparing this field against 4 to assert that inbound traffic is blocked therefore fails on a host that does block it.

defaultOutboundAction.name: defaultOutboundAction
defaultOutboundAction.title: Configured default action for outbound traffic
defaultOutboundAction.desc: One of 0 (not configured), 2 (allow) or 4 (block). As with the inbound action, 0 means no policy sets it and the built-in default applies, which for outbound traffic is allow.

enableStealthModeForIPsec.name: enableStealthModeForIPsec
enableStealthModeForIPsec.title: Whether to use stealth mode for IPsec-protected traffic

enabled.name: enabled
enabled.title: Whether the firewall is enabled on this profile (1 = enabled, 0 = disabled)

logFileName.name: logFileName
logFileName.title: Filename in which to store the firewall log

logIgnored.name: logIgnored
logIgnored.title: Whether to log an event when rules are ignored

logMaxSizeKilobytes.name: logMaxSizeKilobytes
logMaxSizeKilobytes.title: Maximum size the log file can reach before being rotated, in kilobytes

name.name: name
name.title: Name of the profile (Domain, Private, or Public)

notifyOnListen.name: notifyOnListen
notifyOnListen.title: Whether to notify users when an application listens on a port that is closed

windows.firewall.profile.title: Windows Firewall profile entry
windows.firewall.profile.desc: Per-profile firewall settings for one of the three Windows Firewall profiles (Domain, Private, Public): whether the firewall is enabled, default inbound and outbound actions, local rule merge policies, unicast response behavior, stealth mode for IPsec, and log settings including max log size, allowed/blocked packet logging, and log file name.

windows.firewall.rule.name: windows.firewall.rule

action.name: action
action.title: Specifies the action to take on traffic that matches this rule
action.desc: Values: block, allow, or allow only if secure (reported as the integer action code returned by Get-NetFirewallRule).

authorizedComputers.name: authorizedComputers
authorizedComputers.title: Authorized remote computers
authorizedComputers.desc: The literal `Any` when the rule places no machine condition on the traffic it permits. Otherwise an SDDL security descriptor restricting the rule to connections from authenticated remote machines that match it. Null when the host reported no security condition for the rule.

authorizedUsers.name: authorizedUsers
authorizedUsers.title: Authorized remote users
authorizedUsers.desc: The literal `Any` when the rule places no user condition on the traffic it permits, which is the case for every rule a stock Windows install ships with. Otherwise an SDDL security descriptor restricting the rule to connections whose authenticated remote user matches it. Null when the host reported no security condition for the rule.

direction.name: direction
direction.title: Specifies which direction of traffic to match with this rule

displayGroup.name: displayGroup
displayGroup.title: The group that this rule belongs to

edgeTraversalPolicy.name: edgeTraversalPolicy
edgeTraversalPolicy.title: Specifies how this firewall rule will handle edge traversal cases
edgeTraversalPolicy.desc: Values: block (0), allow (1), defer to user (2), defer to app (3).

enabled.name: enabled
enabled.title: Whether this rule is administratively enabled or disabled

enforcementStatus.name: enforcementStatus
enforcementStatus.title: How the firewall enforces the rule
enforcementStatus.desc: One or more enforcement states, for example `Enforced`. A rule with several has them joined with ", " (for example `DisabledInProfile, ProfileInactive, Enforced`).

icmpTypes.name: icmpTypes
icmpTypes.title: ICMP types and codes the rule matches
icmpTypes.desc: Each entry is either a type number such as `8`, a `type:code` pair such as `3:4`, or the literal `Any`. Rules whose protocol is not ICMP report `Any` rather than an empty list, so read this together with `protocol`.

instanceID.name: instanceID
instanceID.title: A string that uniquely identifies this instance within the policy store

interfaceTypes.name: interfaceTypes
interfaceTypes.title: Interface types the rule applies to
interfaceTypes.desc: Any combination of `Wired`, `Wireless`, and `RemoteAccess`, or the single value `Any`.

localAddresses.name: localAddresses
localAddresses.title: Local addresses the rule matches
localAddresses.desc: Individual addresses, CIDR blocks, inclusive ranges, or the literal `Any`.

localOnlyMapping.name: localOnlyMapping
localOnlyMapping.title: Whether to group UDP packets into conversations based only on the local address and port

localPorts.name: localPorts
localPorts.title: Local ports the rule matches
localPorts.desc: Individual ports, inclusive ranges such as `8554-8558`, the literal `Any`, or one of the dynamic keywords Windows accepts in place of a port number (`RPC`, `RPCEPMap`, `IPHTTPS`, `PlayToDiscovery`).

looseSourceMapping.name: looseSourceMapping
looseSourceMapping.title: Whether to group UDP packets into conversations based on the local address, local port, and remote port

policyStoreSource.name: policyStoreSource
policyStoreSource.title: Policy store the rule came from
policyStoreSource.desc: The name of the Group Policy object that delivered the rule, or PersistentStore for a rule configured locally.

policyStoreSourceType.name: policyStoreSourceType
policyStoreSourceType.title: Type of the policy store the rule came from

primaryStatus.name: primaryStatus
primaryStatus.title: PrimaryStatus provides a high level status value

profiles.name: profiles
profiles.title: Firewall profiles this rule applies to
profiles.desc: Any combination of `Domain`, `Private`, and `Public`, or the single value `Any` when the rule applies to every profile. A rule only takes effect while one of its profiles is the active one, so a permissive rule scoped to `Domain` is a different exposure from the same rule scoped to `Public`.

program.name: program
program.title: Path of the program the rule is scoped to
program.desc: An absolute path, the literal `Any` when the rule applies to every program, or `System` for kernel-mode traffic. Null when the host reported no application condition for the rule.

protocol.name: protocol
protocol.title: IP protocol the rule matches
protocol.desc: A well-known name such as `TCP`, `UDP`, `ICMPv4`, or `ICMPv6`, the literal `Any`, or the IANA protocol number for protocols with no well-known name.

remoteAddresses.name: remoteAddresses
remoteAddresses.title: Remote addresses the rule matches
remoteAddresses.desc: Individual addresses, CIDR blocks, inclusive ranges, the literal `Any`, or one of the address keywords Windows resolves at evaluation time (`LocalSubnet`, `Internet`, `Intranet`, `DNS`, `DHCP`, `WINS`, `DefaultGateway`, `PlayToDevice`). An inbound allow rule whose remote addresses are `Any` accepts traffic from anywhere that can reach the host.

serviceName.name: serviceName
serviceName.title: Windows service the rule is scoped to
serviceName.desc: The service short name, or the literal `Any` when the rule is not scoped to a service. Null when the host reported no service condition for the rule.

windows.firewall.rule.title: Windows Firewall rule entry
windows.firewall.rule.desc: Single Windows Firewall rule: its unique `instanceID`, display name, description, group, enabled state, traffic direction (inbound/ outbound), action (allow/block), edge traversal policy, and enforcement status, together with the conditions the rule matches on: protocol, local and remote ports and addresses, ICMP types, program, service, profiles, interface types, and authorized remote principals. Iterated from `windows.firewall.rules` to audit which rules are active and what traffic they actually permit, for example an enabled inbound allow rule whose remote addresses are `Any`. The condition fields are joined onto the rule from the `Get-NetFirewallPortFilter`, `Get-NetFirewallAddressFilter`, `Get-NetFirewallApplicationFilter`, `Get-NetFirewallServiceFilter`, `Get-NetFirewallInterfaceTypeFilter`, and `Get-NetFirewallSecurityFilter` cmdlets.

windows.hotfix.name: windows.hotfix

description.name: description
description.title: Type of hotfix (e.g., Update or Security Update)

installedOn.name: installedOn
installedOn.title: Date when the hotfix was installed

windows.hotfix.title: Windows hotfix
windows.hotfix.desc: Single installed Windows hotfix (a Quick Fix Engineering update): its `hotfixId` (for example "KB5034441"), the `description` type of the fix, the knowledge-base `caption` URL, the `installedOn` date, and the account that installed it. Audit patch compliance across `windows.hotfixes`, for example `windows.hotfixes.where(installedOn > time.now - 30*time.day)`.

windows.logonSession.name: windows.logonSession

accountDomain.name: accountDomain
accountDomain.title: Domain of the account the session authenticated as
accountDomain.desc: The machine name for a local account, the domain name for a domain account, and "NT AUTHORITY" for the accounts the system creates.

accountName.name: accountName
accountName.title: Account name the session authenticated as

logonId.name: logonId
logonId.title: Locally unique identifier the Local Security Authority assigned
logonId.desc: The decimal low part of the LUID, which is the form WMI reports, for example "999" for the session the system creates at boot. Tools that print the same identifier in hex show that one as 0x3e7. Unique for the life of the boot, and reused after a restart, so it identifies a session within one scan rather than over time.

logonType.name: logonType
logonType.title: How the session was established
logonType.desc: 2 interactive, 3 network, 4 batch, 5 service, 7 unlock, 8 network cleartext, 9 new credentials, 10 remote interactive, 11 cached interactive.

logonTypeName.name: logonTypeName
logonTypeName.title: Readable form of logonType
logonTypeName.desc: For example "RemoteInteractive" for type 10. Empty for a type outside the documented set, in which case read logonType directly.

sid.name: sid
sid.title: Security identifier of the account the session authenticated as
sid.desc: Empty when the account could not be translated to a SID, which happens for a domain account while the domain is unreachable.

startTime.name: startTime
startTime.title: When the session started
startTime.desc: Null when the Local Security Authority reports no start time, which is normal for some of the sessions the system creates at boot.

user.name: user
user.title: Local user account the session authenticated as
user.desc: Matched on `sid`, so it resolves only for an account that exists on this machine. Null for a domain account, for the accounts the system creates, and when the SID could not be translated. Read `accountName` and `accountDomain` to identify a session whose account is not local.

windows.logonSession.title: Windows logon session
windows.logonSession.desc: Single active logon session as the Local Security Authority reports it: the `logonType` that created it, the `authenticationPackage` that authenticated it, the account it runs as, and when it started. `logonType` and its readable form `logonTypeName` carry most of the audit value, since a session's type says how it was established: 10 is an incoming Remote Desktop logon, 3 is a network logon, and 9 is a session created with alternate credentials. `authenticationPackage` reports whether the session was authenticated with Kerberos or fell back to NTLM.

windows.lsa.name: windows.lsa

crashOnAuditFail.name: crashOnAuditFail
crashOnAuditFail.title: Behavior when security audits cannot be logged (Lsa\CrashOnAuditFail)
crashOnAuditFail.desc: Backs the "Audit: Shut down system immediately if unable to log security audits" security option: 0 off, the system keeps running when it cannot write to the Security log; 1 on, the system halts with a Stop error when an event cannot be written to the Security log; 2 set by Windows after such a halt, in which case only members of the Administrators group can log on until an administrator clears the Security log and resets the value. Null when the value is absent, in which case the Windows default of 0 (off) applies rather than a configured 0.

disableDomainCreds.name: disableDomainCreds
disableDomainCreds.title: Whether storing network authentication credentials is disabled (Lsa\DisableDomainCreds)

everyoneIncludesAnonymous.name: everyoneIncludesAnonymous
everyoneIncludesAnonymous.title: Whether the Everyone permissions apply to anonymous users (Lsa\EveryoneIncludesAnonymous)

fipsAlgorithmPolicyEnabled.name: fipsAlgorithmPolicyEnabled
fipsAlgorithmPolicyEnabled.title: Whether FIPS compliant algorithms are required for encryption, hashing, and signing (Lsa\FipsAlgorithmPolicy\Enabled)
fipsAlgorithmPolicyEnabled.desc: Backs the "System cryptography: Use FIPS compliant algorithms for encryption, hashing, and signing" security option. When enabled, Windows components restrict themselves to FIPS 140 validated algorithms. Null when the value is absent, in which case the Windows default of FIPS mode off applies rather than a configured false.

forceGuest.name: forceGuest
forceGuest.title: Whether the guest-only sharing and security model is used for local accounts (Lsa\ForceGuest)

kerberosAllowsAes128.name: kerberosAllowsAes128
kerberosAllowsAes128.title: Whether Kerberos may negotiate AES128-CTS-HMAC-SHA1-96 (bit 0x8 of SupportedEncryptionTypes)
kerberosAllowsAes128.desc: Decoded from kerberosSupportedEncryptionTypes. Null when that value is absent, in which case Windows uses its built-in default set rather than a configured one.

kerberosAllowsAes256.name: kerberosAllowsAes256
kerberosAllowsAes256.title: Whether Kerberos may negotiate AES256-CTS-HMAC-SHA1-96 (bit 0x10 of SupportedEncryptionTypes)
kerberosAllowsAes256.desc: Decoded from kerberosSupportedEncryptionTypes. Null when that value is absent, in which case Windows uses its built-in default set rather than a configured one.

kerberosAllowsDesCbcCrc.name: kerberosAllowsDesCbcCrc
kerberosAllowsDesCbcCrc.title: Whether Kerberos may negotiate the legacy DES-CBC-CRC cipher (bit 0x1 of SupportedEncryptionTypes)
kerberosAllowsDesCbcCrc.desc: DES is broken and a hardened system leaves this bit clear. Decoded from kerberosSupportedEncryptionTypes. Null when that value is absent, in which case Windows uses its built-in default set rather than a configured one.

kerberosAllowsDesCbcMd5.name: kerberosAllowsDesCbcMd5
kerberosAllowsDesCbcMd5.title: Whether Kerberos may negotiate the legacy DES-CBC-MD5 cipher (bit 0x2 of SupportedEncryptionTypes)
kerberosAllowsDesCbcMd5.desc: DES is broken and a hardened system leaves this bit clear. Decoded from kerberosSupportedEncryptionTypes. Null when that value is absent, in which case Windows uses its built-in default set rather than a configured one.

kerberosAllowsRc4Hmac.name: kerberosAllowsRc4Hmac
kerberosAllowsRc4Hmac.title: Whether Kerberos may negotiate the legacy RC4-HMAC-MD5 cipher (bit 0x4 of SupportedEncryptionTypes)
kerberosAllowsRc4Hmac.desc: RC4 is retained only as a transition fallback and is the cipher targeted by Kerberoasting. A hardened system leaves this bit clear. Decoded from kerberosSupportedEncryptionTypes. Null when that value is absent, in which case Windows uses its built-in default set rather than a configured one.

kerberosSupportedEncryptionTypes.name: kerberosSupportedEncryptionTypes
kerberosSupportedEncryptionTypes.title: Kerberos encryption types the computer is allowed to negotiate (SupportedEncryptionTypes bitmask)
kerberosSupportedEncryptionTypes.desc:
Bitmask behind the "Network security: Configure encryption types allowed for Kerberos" security option. The defined bits are 0x1 DES_CBC_CRC, 0x2 DES_CBC_MD5, 0x4 RC4_HMAC_MD5, 0x8 AES128_CTS_HMAC_SHA1_96, 0x10 AES256_CTS_HMAC_SHA1_96, and 0x20 AES256_CTS_HMAC_SHA1_96_SK, with the remaining high bits reserved for future encryption types. A common hardened value is 0x7FFFFFF8, which clears the three legacy bits and leaves the rest set.

Read from the policy location SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Policies\System\Kerberos\Parameters. Up to Windows Server 2022 the legacy location Lsa\Kerberos\Parameters is read as a fallback when the policy value is absent. Windows Server 2025 (build 26100) no longer honors that location at all, so on that release and later it is not consulted and a value left there by an older hardening script does not appear here: it is inert on the host, and reporting it would describe a configuration Windows is not applying. Null when no honored location carries the value, in which case Windows uses its built-in default set rather than a configured 0. The kerberosAllows fields decode the well-known bits, since MQL has no bitwise operators to test them with.

ldapClientIntegrity.name: ldapClientIntegrity
ldapClientIntegrity.title: LDAP client signing requirement (Services\LDAP\LDAPClientIntegrity)
ldapClientIntegrity.desc: Backs the "Network security: LDAP client signing requirements" security option, which controls whether this computer requests or requires signing when it binds to an LDAP server: 0 none, 1 negotiate signing, 2 require signing. Null when the value is absent, in which case the Windows default applies rather than a configured 0.

ldapEnforceChannelBinding.name: ldapEnforceChannelBinding
ldapEnforceChannelBinding.title: LDAP server channel binding token requirement (Services\NTDS\Parameters\LdapEnforceChannelBinding)
ldapEnforceChannelBinding.desc: Extended Protection for Authentication enforcement on LDAP over TLS binds, introduced by ADV190023: 0 never, 1 when supported, 2 always required. The NTDS key exists only on domain controllers, so this resolves to null on a member server or a standalone host where the setting does not apply, and also on a domain controller that never configured the value. Null therefore means the Windows default is in force, not that channel binding is off.

ldapServerIntegrity.name: ldapServerIntegrity
ldapServerIntegrity.title: LDAP server signing requirement (Services\NTDS\Parameters\LDAPServerIntegrity)
ldapServerIntegrity.desc: Backs the "Domain controller: LDAP server signing requirements" security option, which controls whether the directory rejects unsigned LDAP binds: 0 and 1 both leave unsigned binds acceptable, 2 requires signing. The NTDS key exists only on domain controllers, so this resolves to null on a member server or a standalone host where the setting does not apply, and also on a domain controller that never configured the value. Null therefore means the Windows default is in force, not that signing is not required.

limitBlankPasswordUse.name: limitBlankPasswordUse
limitBlankPasswordUse.title: Whether local accounts with blank passwords are limited to console logon (Lsa\LimitBlankPasswordUse)

lmCompatibilityLevel.name: lmCompatibilityLevel
lmCompatibilityLevel.title: LAN Manager authentication level (Lsa\LmCompatibilityLevel; 0-5, higher is stronger)
lmCompatibilityLevel.desc: 0 sends LM and NTLM responses; 5 sends NTLMv2 only and refuses LM and NTLM. Higher values are more secure; CIS baselines require 5.

noLmHash.name: noLmHash
noLmHash.title: Whether the LAN Manager (LM) hash of new passwords is not stored (Lsa\NoLMHash)

ntlm.name: ntlm
ntlm.title: NTLM authentication settings (Lsa\MSV1_0 and the WDigest provider)

relaxMinimumPasswordLengthLimits.name: relaxMinimumPasswordLengthLimits
relaxMinimumPasswordLengthLimits.title: Whether a minimum password length above 14 characters may be configured (Control\SAM\RelaxMinimumPasswordLengthLimits)
relaxMinimumPasswordLengthLimits.desc: Backs the "Relax minimum password length limits" password policy setting, read from HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\SAM. When enabled, the Minimum password length policy accepts values greater than 14 characters; when disabled or absent, it is capped at 14. Honored on Windows 10 version 2004, Windows Server version 2004, Windows Server 2022, and later; older releases ignore the value. Null when the value is absent, in which case the Windows default of disabled applies rather than a configured false.

restrictAnonymous.name: restrictAnonymous
restrictAnonymous.title: Restrictions on anonymous (null session) connections (Lsa\RestrictAnonymous; higher is more restrictive)

restrictAnonymousSam.name: restrictAnonymousSam
restrictAnonymousSam.title: Whether anonymous enumeration of SAM accounts is disallowed (Lsa\RestrictAnonymousSAM)

restrictRemoteSam.name: restrictRemoteSam
restrictRemoteSam.title: SDDL string controlling which clients may make remote SAM calls (Lsa\restrictremotesam, REG_SZ)

runAsPpl.name: runAsPpl
runAsPpl.title: LSA protection / Run as Protected Process Light level (Lsa\RunAsPPL; 1 or 2 enables LSA protection)

sceNoApplyLegacyAuditPolicy.name: sceNoApplyLegacyAuditPolicy
sceNoApplyLegacyAuditPolicy.title: Whether advanced audit policy is forced over legacy audit categories (Lsa\SCENoApplyLegacyAuditPolicy)
sceNoApplyLegacyAuditPolicy.desc: When set, the advanced audit policy subcategories are forced and the legacy audit categories are ignored.

submitControl.name: submitControl
submitControl.title: Whether recovery console authority delegation submit-control is allowed (Lsa\SubmitControl)

useMachineId.name: useMachineId
useMachineId.title: Whether the computer account identity is used for outbound authentication (Lsa\UseMachineId)

windows.lsa.title: Windows Local Security Authority (LSA) security policy
windows.lsa.desc: Local Security Authority configuration that backs the "Network access", "Network security", and related security options under HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Lsa. These values control anonymous access restrictions, blank-password use, LAN Manager authentication level, NTLM hashing, LSA protection (RunAsPPL), and audit behavior, including whether the system halts when it cannot write security audits. On/off settings are exposed as booleans and graded settings (such as the LAN Manager authentication level) as integers. NTLM (MSV1_0 and WDigest) settings are grouped under `ntlm` and the Netlogon secure-channel settings under `secureChannel`. The FIPS algorithm policy, the Kerberos supported encryption types, the LDAP signing and channel-binding requirements, and the Security Accounts Manager (SAM) minimum password length limit are read from their own keys and exposed directly on this resource. Values are nullable: an absent value resolves to null so it is distinguishable from an explicit false or 0, letting checks assert on configured-vs-default precisely.

windows.lsa.ntlm.name: windows.lsa.ntlm

allowNullSessionFallback.name: allowNullSessionFallback
allowNullSessionFallback.title: Whether NTLM NULL session fallback is allowed (MSV1_0\AllowNullSessionFallback)

allowOnlineId.name: allowOnlineId
allowOnlineId.title: Whether online identities (PKU2U) may authenticate to this computer (Lsa\pku2u\AllowOnlineID)

auditReceivingNtlmTraffic.name: auditReceivingNtlmTraffic
auditReceivingNtlmTraffic.title: Audit level for incoming NTLM traffic (MSV1_0\AuditReceivingNTLMTraffic; 0 off, 1 allow, 2 deny-all)

ntlmMinClientSec.name: ntlmMinClientSec
ntlmMinClientSec.title: Minimum session security negotiated for NTLM SSP clients (MSV1_0\NTLMMinClientSec, bitmask)

ntlmMinServerSec.name: ntlmMinServerSec
ntlmMinServerSec.title: Minimum session security negotiated for NTLM SSP servers (MSV1_0\NTLMMinServerSec, bitmask)

restrictSendingNtlmTraffic.name: restrictSendingNtlmTraffic
restrictSendingNtlmTraffic.title: Restriction level for outgoing NTLM traffic to remote servers (MSV1_0\RestrictSendingNTLMTraffic; 0 allow, 1 audit, 2 deny-all)

useLogonCredential.name: useLogonCredential
useLogonCredential.title: Whether WDigest caches plaintext credentials in memory (WDigest\UseLogonCredential)
useLogonCredential.desc: When enabled, WDigest keeps clear-text passwords in LSASS memory where credential-theft tools can read them. The hardened state is false (0).

windows.lsa.ntlm.title: Windows LSA NTLM authentication settings
windows.lsa.ntlm.desc: NTLM security settings under HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Lsa\MSV1_0 together with the WDigest provider's UseLogonCredential value under HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\SecurityProviders\WDigest. These control NULL session fallback, inbound/outbound NTLM auditing and restriction, the minimum negotiated NTLM session security for clients and servers, and whether WDigest caches plaintext credentials in memory. On/off settings are exposed as booleans and graded settings (audit and restriction levels, the minimum-session-security bitmasks) as integers. Values are nullable so an absent value is distinguishable from an explicit false or 0.

windows.lsa.secureChannel.name: windows.lsa.secureChannel

auditNtlmInDomain.name: auditNtlmInDomain
auditNtlmInDomain.title: Audit level for inbound NTLM traffic on domain controllers (Netlogon\Parameters\AuditNTLMInDomain, bitmask)

blockNetbiosDiscovery.name: blockNetbiosDiscovery
blockNetbiosDiscovery.title: Whether NetBIOS-based domain controller discovery is blocked (Policies\Microsoft\Netlogon\Parameters\BlockNetbiosDiscovery)

disablePasswordChange.name: disablePasswordChange
disablePasswordChange.title: Whether automatic machine account password changes are disabled (Netlogon\Parameters\DisablePasswordChange)

maximumPasswordAge.name: maximumPasswordAge
maximumPasswordAge.title: Maximum machine account password age in days (Netlogon\Parameters\MaximumPasswordAge)

refusePasswordChange.name: refusePasswordChange
refusePasswordChange.title: Whether the domain controller refuses machine account password changes (Netlogon\Parameters\RefusePasswordChange)

requireSignOrSeal.name: requireSignOrSeal
requireSignOrSeal.title: Whether secure-channel data is digitally signed or sealed when possible (Netlogon\Parameters\RequireSignOrSeal)

requireStrongKey.name: requireStrongKey
requireStrongKey.title: Whether a strong (128-bit) secure-channel session key is required (Netlogon\Parameters\RequireStrongKey)

sealSecureChannel.name: sealSecureChannel
sealSecureChannel.title: Whether secure-channel data is digitally encrypted when possible (Netlogon\Parameters\SealSecureChannel)

signSecureChannel.name: signSecureChannel
signSecureChannel.title: Whether secure-channel data is digitally signed when possible (Netlogon\Parameters\SignSecureChannel)

vulnerableChannelAllowList.name: vulnerableChannelAllowList
vulnerableChannelAllowList.title: Allow list of vulnerable Netlogon secure channels (Netlogon\Parameters\vulnerablechannelallowlist, REG_SZ)
vulnerableChannelAllowList.desc: Machine names exempted from secure RPC enforcement (Zerologon / CVE-2020-1472 mitigation). A hardened system has an empty allow list.

windows.lsa.secureChannel.title: Windows LSA Netlogon secure-channel settings
windows.lsa.secureChannel.desc: Netlogon secure-channel (domain member) settings under HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Services\Netlogon\Parameters. These control digital signing and sealing of secure-channel data, the machine account password change behavior and maximum age, strong session keys, NETBIOS discovery, the vulnerable-channel allow list, and inbound NTLM auditing in the domain. BlockNetbiosDiscovery is read from the GPO location HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Netlogon\Parameters. On/off settings are exposed as booleans and graded settings (the inbound NTLM audit bitmask and the maximum password age) as integers. Values are nullable so an absent value is distinguishable from an explicit false or 0.

windows.optionalFeature.name: windows.optionalFeature

description.name: description
description.title: Feature description
description.desc: Loaded on demand: DISM only reports it for a named feature, which costs an extra image query.

displayName.name: displayName
displayName.title: Human-readable display name of the feature
displayName.desc: Loaded on demand: DISM only reports it for a named feature, which costs an extra image query.

enabled.name: enabled
enabled.title: Whether the feature is enabled

name.name: name
name.title: Feature name (ID) of the optional feature (for example "SMB1Protocol")

state.name: state
state.title: Feature state
state.desc: The DISM feature state: 0 = Disabled, 1 = Disable pending, 2 = Enabled, 3 = Enable pending (a pending state takes effect after the next reboot). Read `enabled` rather than comparing this to a number.

windows.optionalFeature.title: Windows optional feature (desktop-only)
windows.optionalFeature.desc: Windows optional feature reported by `Get-WindowsOptionalFeature -Online`, the desktop equivalent of server roles. Select one by its feature name, for example `windows.optionalFeature(name: "SMB1Protocol")`, to check whether a legacy or risky feature (such as SMBv1, Telnet client, or PowerShell v2) is turned on. `enabled` is the simple boolean; `state` carries the underlying DISM feature state for more granular checks.

windows.powershell.name: windows.powershell

executionPolicy.name: executionPolicy
executionPolicy.title: PowerShell execution policy (PowerShell\ExecutionPolicy)
executionPolicy.desc: The machine-wide execution policy string set by Group Policy, e.g. "AllSigned", "RemoteSigned", or "Restricted". Null when the value is absent.

languageMode.name: languageMode
languageMode.title: PowerShell language mode implied by the system lockdown state
languageMode.desc: "ConstrainedLanguage" when `lockdownPolicy` requests enforcement, otherwise "FullLanguage". Audit reports "FullLanguage" because it records what would have been blocked without restricting the session, so read `lockdownPolicy` to tell audit apart from no lockdown at all. Null when `lockdownPolicy` is null: this field covers only the `__PSLockdownPolicy` fall-back, and a host constrained by an active App Control or AppLocker policy leaves that value unset.

lockdownPolicy.name: lockdownPolicy
lockdownPolicy.title: System lockdown state (__PSLockdownPolicy)
lockdownPolicy.desc: The machine-scoped `__PSLockdownPolicy` environment variable, read from HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Session Manager\Environment. PowerShell reads it as a Windows Lockdown Policy state bitmask when no App Control or AppLocker policy applies: the 0x8 bit requests audit and the 0x4 bit requests enforcement, and enforcement runs sessions in ConstrainedLanguage mode. Null when the value is absent or does not parse as a number, which is the default on a host with no lockdown configured.

windows.powershell.title: Windows PowerShell logging policy
windows.powershell.desc: PowerShell logging settings configured via Group Policy under HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\PowerShell: Script Block Logging, Module Logging, Transcription, and the machine execution policy, together with the system lockdown state that decides the session language mode. The policy settings are GPO-only values with no effective fallback, so when a value is absent the corresponding field is null, which is distinguishable from an explicit 0. Read from the registry, so it is available even on connections that cannot run commands.

windows.powershell.moduleLogging.name: windows.powershell.moduleLogging

enabled.name: enabled
enabled.title: Whether module logging is enabled (EnableModuleLogging); null when the value is absent

moduleNames.name: moduleNames
moduleNames.title: Module names selected for logging (ModuleNames subkey)
moduleNames.desc: One entry per module named by the policy, taken from the value names under the ModuleNames subkey. A single entry of "*" selects every module. Null when the ModuleNames subkey is absent, and an empty list when the subkey exists but names no module, in which case module logging records nothing even while `enabled` is true.

windows.powershell.moduleLogging.title: PowerShell Module Logging policy
