windows.powershell.moduleLogging.desc: Module Logging policy under HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft \Windows\PowerShell\ModuleLogging. Module logging records pipeline execution details for the selected modules to the Windows PowerShell event log. The policy carries two halves: whether it is on, and which modules it covers. A policy that is on but names no module logs nothing, so `moduleNames` is what says whether the setting has any effect. This is a GPO-only value; when it is absent the field is null, distinguishable from an explicit 0.

windows.powershell.scriptBlockLogging.name: windows.powershell.scriptBlockLogging

enabled.name: enabled
enabled.title: Whether script block logging is enabled (EnableScriptBlockLogging); null when the value is absent

invocationLogging.name: invocationLogging
invocationLogging.title: Whether script block invocation logging is enabled (EnableScriptBlockInvocationLogging)
invocationLogging.desc: Records an event each time a command, script block, function, or script starts and stops, in addition to the script block contents recorded by `enabled`. It produces a high volume of events, so it is usually left off outside an investigation. Null when the value is absent.

windows.powershell.scriptBlockLogging.title: PowerShell Script Block Logging policy
windows.powershell.scriptBlockLogging.desc: Script Block Logging policy under HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies \Microsoft\Windows\PowerShell\ScriptBlockLogging. Script block logging records the deobfuscated contents of scripts and commands to the event log, a key control for detecting malicious PowerShell. This is a GPO-only value; when it is absent the field is null, distinguishable from an explicit 0.

windows.powershell.transcription.name: windows.powershell.transcription

enableInvocationHeader.name: enableInvocationHeader
enableInvocationHeader.title: Whether each transcribed command carries an invocation header (EnableInvocationHeader)
enableInvocationHeader.desc: Writes a timestamped header before every command recorded in the transcript, which is what makes the transcript usable as a timeline. Null when the value is absent.

enabled.name: enabled
enabled.title: Whether PowerShell transcription is enabled (EnableTranscripting); null when the value is absent

outputDirectory.name: outputDirectory
outputDirectory.title: Directory transcripts are written to (OutputDirectory)
outputDirectory.desc: The directory PowerShell writes session transcripts to. Null when the value is absent, in which case transcripts land in the user's Documents folder on the host that produced them. The path is worth auditing in its own right: a directory writable by unprivileged users lets an attacker edit the record of their own session, and a purely local path leaves the only copy on the machine being investigated.

windows.powershell.transcription.title: PowerShell Transcription policy
windows.powershell.transcription.desc: Transcription policy under HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft \Windows\PowerShell\Transcription. Transcription writes a record of every PowerShell session (input and output) to text files. This is a GPO-only value; when it is absent the field is null, distinguishable from an explicit 0.

configFile.name: configFile
configFile.title: Path of the driver configuration DLL

dataFile.name: dataFile
dataFile.title: Path of the driver data file

environment.name: environment
environment.title: Print environment the driver is registered under, for example "Windows x64"

hardwareId.name: hardwareId
hardwareId.title: Identifier the vendor declares in the driver INF
hardwareId.desc: For example "RICOHPCL6DriveforUP". Unlike name this does not change between releases: Windows uses it to rank and upgrade drivers, so a vendor that changed it would break updates for every existing installation. It is what purl is keyed on. Empty for some drivers, in which case purl falls back to the name.

infPath.name: infPath
infPath.title: Path of the INF the driver package was installed from

modelVersion.name: modelVersion
modelVersion.title: Driver model version: 2, 3 or 4
modelVersion.desc: The spooler interface generation, not the vendor release number. Version 4 drivers are the isolated, package-aware kind.

name.name: name
name.title: Driver name as the spooler reports it

purl.name: purl
purl.title: Package URL identifying this driver
purl.desc: A pkg:windows-driver purl whose namespace is the vendor, for example pkg:windows-driver/ricoh/pcl-6-driver@4.40.0.0. Empty when the spooler reports no manufacturer or no name, because a driver name alone does not identify a driver: "PCL 6 Driver" and "PostScript3 Driver" name page description languages that every printer vendor ships a driver for.

version.name: version
version.title: Vendor driver version in dotted form, for example "3.0.0.0"
version.desc: Windows stores this packed into a single 64-bit integer holding four 16-bit fields. This is the unpacked form vendors publish and advise on, and it is lossless: every field of the packed value appears here. Empty when the spooler reports no version.

windows.printerDrivers.name: windows.printerDrivers
windows.printerDrivers.title: Print drivers registered with the Windows spooler
windows.printerDrivers.desc: Print drivers as the spooler reports them, with the vendor version, the manufacturer, the print environment each is registered under, and the INF the package was installed from. Use it to assert which drivers are present and at which version. Drivers are read from the spooler rather than from installed software, because a driver delivered as an INF/CAB package lands in the driver store and creates no Add/Remove Programs entry, so a software inventory cannot see it while the spooler is still loading it.

windows.rdp.name: windows.rdp

alwaysPromptForPassword.name: alwaysPromptForPassword
alwaysPromptForPassword.title: Whether the user is always prompted for a password on connection (fPromptForPassword)

clipboardServerToClientLevel.name: clipboardServerToClientLevel
clipboardServerToClientLevel.title: Server-to-client clipboard redirection level (SCClipLevel)
clipboardServerToClientLevel.desc: The raw SCClipLevel DWORD. 0 disables clipboard transfers from the server to the client; higher values permit progressively more content. Resolves to 3 (unrestricted) when the policy is not configured.

cloudClipboardIntegrationDisabled.name: cloudClipboardIntegrationDisabled
cloudClipboardIntegrationDisabled.title: Whether RDP Cloud Clipboard integration for server-to-client data transfer is disabled (DisableCloudClipboardIntegration)

comPortRedirectionDisabled.name: comPortRedirectionDisabled
comPortRedirectionDisabled.title: Whether client COM port redirection is disabled (fDisableCcm)

connectionsDenied.name: connectionsDenied
connectionsDenied.title: Whether Remote Desktop connections to this host are denied (fDenyTSConnections)

deleteTempDirsOnExit.name: deleteTempDirsOnExit
deleteTempDirsOnExit.title: Whether temporary folders are deleted when the session exits (DeleteTempDirsOnExit)

driveRedirectionDisabled.name: driveRedirectionDisabled
driveRedirectionDisabled.title: Whether client drive redirection is disabled (fDisableCdm)

endSessionWhenTimeLimitReached.name: endSessionWhenTimeLimitReached
endSessionWhenTimeLimitReached.title: Whether a session is ended rather than disconnected when a time limit is reached (fResetBroken)

locationRedirectionDisabled.name: locationRedirectionDisabled
locationRedirectionDisabled.title: Whether client location redirection is disabled (fDisableLocationRedir)

lptPortRedirectionDisabled.name: lptPortRedirectionDisabled
lptPortRedirectionDisabled.title: Whether client LPT port redirection is disabled (fDisableLPT)

maxDisconnectionTimeMs.name: maxDisconnectionTimeMs
maxDisconnectionTimeMs.title: Time limit in milliseconds for disconnected sessions, 0 to never end them (MaxDisconnectionTime)

maxIdleTimeMs.name: maxIdleTimeMs
maxIdleTimeMs.title: Time limit in milliseconds for active but idle sessions, 0 for no limit (MaxIdleTime)

networkLevelAuthentication.name: networkLevelAuthentication
networkLevelAuthentication.title: Whether Network Level Authentication is required (UserAuthentication)

offerRemoteAssistanceAllowed.name: offerRemoteAssistanceAllowed
offerRemoteAssistanceAllowed.title: Whether offer (unsolicited) Remote Assistance is allowed (fAllowUnsolicited)

passwordSavingDisabled.name: passwordSavingDisabled
passwordSavingDisabled.title: Whether saving of Remote Desktop passwords is disabled (DisablePasswordSaving)
passwordSavingDisabled.desc: A Group Policy-only setting under the Terminal Services policy key. False when no policy sets it, because Windows documents the unconfigured behavior as letting the user save passwords in Remote Desktop Connection.

perSessionTempDirsUsed.name: perSessionTempDirsUsed
perSessionTempDirsUsed.title: Whether per-session temporary folders are used (PerSessionTempDir)

pnpDeviceRedirectionDisabled.name: pnpDeviceRedirectionDisabled
pnpDeviceRedirectionDisabled.title: Whether supported Plug and Play device redirection is disabled (fDisablePNPRedir)

secureRpcRequired.name: secureRpcRequired

The name field is the protocol name as it appears in the registry, spaces included, for example "TLS 1.0" or "Multi-Protocol Unified Hello".

clientConfigured and serverConfigured report whether that side has any override in the registry at all. When a side is not configured, Windows applies its built-in default for the release, so enabled and disabledByDefault for that side are null rather than false.

Windows Server 2022 and later also list the RSAE-PSS entries.

windows.schannel.title: Windows Schannel TLS configuration
windows.schannel.desc:
Schannel (Secure Channel) TLS cipher-suite, supported-group, and signature-algorithm configuration that backs the Microsoft TLS/SSL stack, read from the effective local Schannel store under HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Cryptography\Configuration\Local\SSL. The 00010002 subkey holds the ordered cipher-suite list in its REG_MULTI_SZ `Functions` value and the ordered elliptic-curve / supported-group list in its REG_MULTI_SZ `EccCurves` value, the same list `Get-TlsEccCurve` reports. The 00010003 subkey holds the ordered signature-algorithm list in its REG_MULTI_SZ `Functions` value. On Windows 11 24H2 and Windows Server 2025 the supported-group list is where post-quantum ML-KEM key-exchange groups (for example secp256r1_mlkem768) appear once enabled.

When a key or value is absent (the common case on older Windows, on systems using the default order, and on non-Windows platforms) the list accessors resolve to an empty list and pqcKeyExchangeEnabled resolves to false rather than failing.

The protocols, ciphers, hashes, and keyExchangeAlgorithms lists come from the separate per-algorithm override store under HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\SecurityProviders\SCHANNEL. Windows applies a built-in default to every algorithm that has no override there, and that default differs between Windows releases, so an absent registry value does not mean the algorithm is off. Each list therefore always contains the well-known algorithm names, whether or not the registry mentions them, and reports configured as false with a null enablement for the ones it does not. Write audits against configured and the enablement fields together, for example `windows.schannel.protocols.where(name == "TLS 1.0").all(clientConfigured && clientEnabled == false)`, so a host that never set the value fails instead of passing on a null.

Audit which tasks run, as whom, and on what schedule, for example `windows.scheduledTasks.where(enabled).where(principal.runLevel == "Highest")` surfaces enabled tasks running with the highest available privileges.

Server 2019 and later ship without it. SMBv1 is deprecated and should be disabled.

windows.smb.title: Windows SMB (Server Message Block) server
windows.smb.desc: SMB shares published by the host, active inbound client sessions, and outbound connections to other SMB servers, along with the server and client registry hardening configuration and whether the deprecated SMBv1 driver is still enabled. Backed by the `Get-SmbShare`, `Get-SmbSession`, and `Get-SmbConnection` PowerShell cmdlets plus registry reads.

enableAuthRateLimiter.desc: Maps the EnableAuthRateLimiter DWORD; 1 = enabled. Null when unset.

enableForcedLogoff.name: enableForcedLogoff

enableForcedLogoff.desc: Maps the enableforcedlogoff DWORD; 1 = forced logoff enabled. Null when unset.

enableSecuritySignature.name: enableSecuritySignature

enableSecuritySignature.desc: Maps the EnableSecuritySignature DWORD; 1 = enabled. Null when unset.

invalidAuthenticationDelayMs.name: invalidAuthenticationDelayMs

invalidAuthenticationDelayMs.desc: Maps the InvalidAuthenticationDelayTimeInMs DWORD. Null when unset.

nullSessionShares.desc: The REG_MULTI_SZ NullSessionShares value. Empty when unset; a compliant configuration is an empty list.

requireSecuritySignature.desc: Maps the RequireSecuritySignature DWORD; 1 = required. Null when unset.

restrictNullSessionAccess.name: restrictNullSessionAccess

serverNameHardeningLevel.name: serverNameHardeningLevel

serverNameHardeningLevel.desc: Maps the SMBServerNameHardeningLevel DWORD (0, 1, or 2). Null when unset.

windows.smb.serverConfiguration.title: Windows SMB server configuration

addPrinterDriversRestricted.title: Whether adding printer drivers is restricted to administrators
addPrinterDriversRestricted.desc: Maps the LanMan print provider AddPrinterDrivers value (Control\Print\Providers\LanMan Print Services\Servers\AddPrinterDrivers). Null when not configured.

copyFilesPolicy.name: copyFilesPolicy
copyFilesPolicy.title: Whether the spooler restricts copied files to the Windows color system (Printers\CopyFilesPolicy). Null when not configured

disabled.title: Whether the Print Spooler service is disabled (Start == 4)

httpPrintingDisabled.name: httpPrintingDisabled
httpPrintingDisabled.title: Whether printing over HTTP is disabled (Printers\DisableHTTPPrinting)
httpPrintingDisabled.desc: Defaults to false (HTTP printing allowed) when not configured.

ipp.name: ipp

redirectionGuardPolicy.name: redirectionGuardPolicy
redirectionGuardPolicy.title: Whether Redirection Guard is enabled (Printers\RedirectionguardPolicy). Null when not configured

registerRemoteRpcEndpoint.name: registerRemoteRpcEndpoint

registerRemoteRpcEndpoint.desc: The hardened state is false (the remote RPC endpoint is disabled). Null when not configured.

rpcAuthnLevelPrivacyEnabled.name: rpcAuthnLevelPrivacyEnabled
rpcAuthnLevelPrivacyEnabled.title: Whether incoming RPC connections to the spooler require packet privacy (Control\Print\RpcAuthnLevelPrivacyEnabled)
rpcAuthnLevelPrivacyEnabled.desc: Defaults to true (packet privacy enabled), the modern Windows default, when not configured.

startMode.name: startMode
startMode.title: Print Spooler service start type (HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Services\Spooler\Start)
startMode.desc: One of 2 (Automatic), 3 (Manual), or 4 (Disabled). Null when the value is not present.

webPnpDownloadDisabled.name: webPnpDownloadDisabled
webPnpDownloadDisabled.title: Whether downloading of print drivers over HTTP / Web Point-and-Print is disabled (Printers\DisableWebPnPDownload)
webPnpDownloadDisabled.desc: Defaults to false (downloads allowed) when not configured.

windowsProtectedPrintGroupPolicyState.name: windowsProtectedPrintGroupPolicyState
windowsProtectedPrintGroupPolicyState.title: Whether Windows Protected Print mode is enabled (Printers\WPP\WindowsProtectedPrintGroupPolicyState). Null when not configured

windows.spooler.title: Windows Print Spooler security configuration
windows.spooler.desc:
Hardening-relevant state of the Windows Print Spooler and printing subsystem. The fields are sourced from the Group Policy printer keys under HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows NT\Printers (and its PointAndPrint, RPC, IPP, and WPP subkeys), the machine-wide HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Print key, and the spooler service start configuration under HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Services\Spooler. These controls address the PrintNightmare and related spooler vulnerabilities: whether the service is disabled, whether remote RPC is accepted, and how Point-and-Print driver installation is restricted.

Integer settings that are not present in the registry resolve to null so "not configured" is distinguishable from an explicit value of 0 (important because several controls, for example registerRemoteRpcEndpoint == 0, are compliant precisely when set to 0). Boolean settings resolve to their documented Windows default when the value is absent.

windows.spooler.ipp.name: windows.spooler.ipp

blockCertCNInvalid.name: blockCertCNInvalid
blockCertCNInvalid.title: Whether IPP rejects server certificates whose CN does not match (SecurityFlagsBlockCertCNInvalid)

blockCertDateInvalid.name: blockCertDateInvalid
blockCertDateInvalid.title: Whether IPP rejects expired or not-yet-valid server certificates (SecurityFlagsBlockCertDateInvalid)

blockCertWrongUsage.name: blockCertWrongUsage
blockCertWrongUsage.title: Whether IPP rejects server certificates used for the wrong purpose (SecurityFlagsBlockCertWrongUsage)

blockUnknownCA.name: blockUnknownCA
blockUnknownCA.title: Whether IPP rejects server certificates from an unknown CA (SecurityFlagsBlockUnknownCA)

requireIpps.name: requireIpps
requireIpps.title: Whether IPP connections must use IPP over HTTPS (RequireIpps)
requireIpps.desc: Defaults to false when not configured.

windows.spooler.ipp.title: Windows Print Spooler Internet Printing Protocol (IPP) settings
windows.spooler.ipp.desc: Certificate validation flags under HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows NT\Printers\IPP. The boolean fields report whether each certificate check is enforced; they default to false (the check is not enforced) when the corresponding value is absent.

windows.spooler.pointAndPrint.name: windows.spooler.pointAndPrint

noWarningNoElevationOnInstall.name: noWarningNoElevationOnInstall
noWarningNoElevationOnInstall.title: Whether elevation/warning prompts are suppressed when installing a Point-and-Print driver (NoWarningNoElevationOnInstall)
noWarningNoElevationOnInstall.desc: The hardened state is false (the warning/elevation prompt is kept). Null when not configured.

restrictDriverInstallationToAdministrato.name: restrictDriverInstallationToAdministrators
restrictDriverInstallationToAdministrato.title: Whether printer driver installation is restricted to administrators (RestrictDriverInstallationToAdministrators)
restrictDriverInstallationToAdministrato.desc: Defaults to true (the hardened Windows default introduced by the PrintNightmare mitigations) when not configured.

updatePromptSettings.name: updatePromptSettings
updatePromptSettings.title: Whether to suppress elevation/warning prompts when updating a Point-and-Print driver (UpdatePromptSettings)
updatePromptSettings.desc: 0 keeps the warning/elevation prompt (the hardened state). Null when not configured.

windows.spooler.pointAndPrint.title: Windows Print Spooler Point and Print restrictions
windows.spooler.pointAndPrint.desc: Settings under HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows NT\Printers\PointAndPrint that govern how non-administrators may install printer drivers from a print server. Values are null when not configured.

windows.spooler.rpc.name: windows.spooler.rpc

authentication.title: RPC authentication requirement for incoming connections (RpcAuthentication)
authentication.desc: 1 = default, 2 = negotiate, 3 = none. Null when not configured.

forceKerberos.name: forceKerberos
forceKerberos.title: Whether Kerberos is required for incoming spooler RPC connections (ForceKerberosForRpc)
forceKerberos.desc: Defaults to false when not configured.

protocols.name: protocols
protocols.title: Allowed RPC transport protocols bitmask (RpcProtocols)
protocols.desc: 5 allows RPC over TCP and named pipes; 7 adds local. Null when not configured.

tcpPort.name: tcpPort
tcpPort.title: Fixed TCP port used for RPC over TCP, 0 for dynamic (RpcTcpPort)

useNamedPipeProtocol.name: useNamedPipeProtocol
useNamedPipeProtocol.title: Whether the spooler allows RPC over named pipes in addition to TCP (RpcUseNamedPipeProtocol)
useNamedPipeProtocol.desc: The hardened state is false (RPC over TCP only). Null when not configured.

windows.spooler.rpc.title: Windows Print Spooler RPC settings
windows.spooler.rpc.desc: Settings under HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows NT\Printers\RPC that control the transport and authentication used for spooler RPC. Integer values are null when not configured.

windows.telemetry.name: windows.telemetry

allowTelemetry.name: allowTelemetry
allowTelemetry.title: Diagnostic data level (DataCollection\AllowTelemetry): 0=Security, 1=Basic/Required, 2=Enhanced, 3=Full. Null when not configured.

disableCloudOptimizedContent.name: disableCloudOptimizedContent
disableCloudOptimizedContent.title: Whether cloud-optimized content is disabled (CloudContent\DisableCloudOptimizedContent)
disableCloudOptimizedContent.desc: Cloud-optimized content tailors suggestions using cloud data. Null when the policy is not configured.

disableConsumerAccountStateContent.name: disableConsumerAccountStateContent
disableConsumerAccountStateContent.title: Whether consumer account state content is disabled (CloudContent\DisableConsumerAccountStateContent). Null when not configured.

disableEnterpriseAuthProxy.name: disableEnterpriseAuthProxy
disableEnterpriseAuthProxy.title: Whether the telemetry service may not use an authenticated proxy (DataCollection\DisableEnterpriseAuthProxy)
disableEnterpriseAuthProxy.desc: Applies to the Connected User Experiences and Telemetry service. Null when the policy is not configured.

disableOneSettingsDownloads.name: disableOneSettingsDownloads
disableOneSettingsDownloads.title: Whether downloading configuration from the OneSettings service is disabled (DataCollection\DisableOneSettingsDownloads). Null when not configured.

disableWindowsConsumerFeatures.name: disableWindowsConsumerFeatures
disableWindowsConsumerFeatures.title: Whether Windows consumer features are disabled (CloudContent\DisableWindowsConsumerFeatures)
disableWindowsConsumerFeatures.desc: Consumer features include app suggestions and consumer experiences. Null when the policy is not configured.

doNotShowFeedbackNotifications.name: doNotShowFeedbackNotifications
doNotShowFeedbackNotifications.title: Whether feedback notifications are suppressed (DataCollection\DoNotShowFeedbackNotifications)
doNotShowFeedbackNotifications.desc: When set, the user does not receive telemetry feedback notifications. Null when the policy is not configured.

enableOneSettingsAuditing.name: enableOneSettingsAuditing
enableOneSettingsAuditing.title: Whether auditing of OneSettings usage is enabled (DataCollection\EnableOneSettingsAuditing). Null when not configured.

limitDiagnosticLogCollection.name: limitDiagnosticLogCollection
limitDiagnosticLogCollection.title: Whether collection of diagnostic logs is limited (DataCollection\LimitDiagnosticLogCollection). Null when not configured.

limitDumpCollection.name: limitDumpCollection
limitDumpCollection.title: Whether collection of crash dumps is limited (DataCollection\LimitDumpCollection). Null when not configured.

windows.telemetry.title: Windows diagnostic data (telemetry) and consumer cloud-content policy
windows.telemetry.desc: Effective Windows privacy and telemetry posture read from the Group Policy keys HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\DataCollection and HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\CloudContent. These are GPO-only DWORD values. The diagnostic data level is a graded integer; the remaining settings are on/off booleans. Every field is nullable so that an absent value (the policy is not configured) is distinguishable from an explicit false or 0. Read from the registry, so it is available even on connections that cannot run commands.

windows.tpm.name: windows.tpm

autoProvisioning.name: autoProvisioning
autoProvisioning.title: Whether Windows automatically provisions the TPM
autoProvisioning.desc: One of Enabled, Disabled, EnabledForCertainOnly, or NotDefined, and empty when the TPM reports nothing at all. Automatic provisioning is what makes a TPM ready for use without an administrator preparing it, and disabling it leaves a present TPM unusable by BitLocker and device health attestation. A machine with no TPM reports NotDefined.

enabled.name: enabled
enabled.title: Whether the TPM is enabled

lockedOut.name: lockedOut
lockedOut.title: Whether the TPM is locked out against dictionary attack
lockedOut.desc: True after too many failed authorization attempts, while the TPM refuses further owner authorization until the lockout heals or is reset.

lockoutCount.name: lockoutCount
lockoutCount.title: Number of authorization failures counted against the lockout threshold

lockoutHealTime.name: lockoutHealTime
lockoutHealTime.title: Time the TPM takes to forget one authorization failure
lockoutHealTime.desc: A human-readable duration such as "2 hours", empty when the TPM reports none. The counter drops by one each time this elapses, so it is how long a lockout takes to clear on its own.

manufacturerId.name: manufacturerId
manufacturerId.title: TPM manufacturer identifier as a number
manufacturerId.desc: The raw TCG vendor identifier, which is usually four ASCII characters packed into an integer. Read `manufacturerIdTxt` for the readable form.

manufacturerIdTxt.name: manufacturerIdTxt
manufacturerIdTxt.title: TPM manufacturer identifier as text, for example "INTC" or "AMD"

ownerClearDisabled.name: ownerClearDisabled
ownerClearDisabled.title: Whether clearing the TPM from the operating system is blocked
ownerClearDisabled.desc: True when the owner authorization needed to clear the TPM is not available to Windows, so a clear has to be confirmed from firmware. Read it together with `present`: a machine with no TPM also reports true, and on its own that reads like hardening on a host that has no TPM to harden.

present.name: present
present.title: Whether a TPM is present on the system

ready.name: ready
ready.title: Whether the TPM is ready for use

specVersion.name: specVersion
specVersion.title: Major TPM specification version, for example "2.0"

windows.tpm.title: Windows Trusted Platform Module (TPM)
windows.tpm.desc: Trusted Platform Module state: whether a TPM is present, ready for use, enabled, and activated, along with its manufacturer, its major specification version, its dictionary-attack lockout state, and whether Windows provisions it automatically. Presence and a 2.0 specification version are prerequisites for Windows 11 readiness and several BitLocker and device-health controls, and a locked out or unprovisioned TPM is present without being usable. On a system without a TPM the fields resolve cleanly (present is false) rather than erroring.

windows.uac.name: windows.uac

consentPromptBehaviorAdmin.name: consentPromptBehaviorAdmin
consentPromptBehaviorAdmin.title: Elevation prompt behavior for administrators in Admin Approval Mode (ConsentPromptBehaviorAdmin)
consentPromptBehaviorAdmin.desc: Backs "User Account Control: Behavior of the elevation prompt for administrators in Admin Approval Mode": 0 elevate without prompting, 1 prompt for credentials on the secure desktop, 2 prompt for consent on the secure desktop, 3 prompt for credentials, 4 prompt for consent, 5 prompt for consent for non-Windows binaries. 0 is the insecure setting. A value outside 0 to 5 is reported as read, since Windows defines no meaning for it. Null when the value is absent, in which case the Windows default of 5 applies.

consentPromptBehaviorUser.name: consentPromptBehaviorUser
consentPromptBehaviorUser.title: Elevation prompt behavior for standard users (ConsentPromptBehaviorUser)
consentPromptBehaviorUser.desc: Backs "User Account Control: Behavior of the elevation prompt for standard users": 0 automatically deny elevation requests, 1 prompt for credentials on the secure desktop, 3 prompt for credentials. Windows defines no meaning for 2 or for any other value, which is reported as read. Null when the value is absent, in which case the Windows default of 3 applies.

enableInstallerDetection.name: enableInstallerDetection
enableInstallerDetection.title: Whether application installations are detected and prompted for elevation (EnableInstallerDetection)
enableInstallerDetection.desc: Backs "User Account Control: Detect application installations and prompt for elevation". Null when the value is absent, in which case the Windows default depends on the edition: enabled on Home editions, disabled on enterprise editions. Windows Server 2016 and 2022 write the value as 1.

enableLua.name: enableLua
enableLua.title: Whether Admin Approval Mode is turned on for all administrators (EnableLUA)
enableLua.desc: Backs "User Account Control: Run all administrators in Admin Approval Mode". When false, Admin Approval Mode and every other UAC policy setting are disabled. Null when the value is absent, in which case the Windows default of enabled applies. A change takes effect after a restart.

enableSecureUiaPaths.name: enableSecureUiaPaths
enableSecureUiaPaths.title: Whether only UIAccess applications installed in secure locations are elevated (EnableSecureUIAPaths)
enableSecureUiaPaths.desc: Backs "User Account Control: Only elevate UIAccess applications that are installed in secure locations". The secure locations are Program Files, Program Files (x86), and Windows\system32. Null when the value is absent, in which case the Windows default of enabled applies.

enableUiaDesktopToggle.name: enableUiaDesktopToggle
enableUiaDesktopToggle.title: Whether UIAccess applications may prompt for elevation without the secure desktop (EnableUIADesktopToggle)
enableUiaDesktopToggle.desc: Backs "User Account Control: Allow UIAccess applications to prompt for elevation without using the secure desktop". When true, UIAccess programs such as Remote Assistance can disable the secure desktop for elevation prompts. Null when the value is absent, in which case the Windows default of disabled applies.

enableVirtualization.name: enableVirtualization
enableVirtualization.title: Whether file and registry write failures are virtualized to per-user locations (EnableVirtualization)
enableVirtualization.desc: Backs "User Account Control: Virtualize file and registry write failures to per-user locations". Null when the value is absent, in which case the Windows default of enabled applies.

filterAdministratorToken.name: filterAdministratorToken
filterAdministratorToken.title: Whether Admin Approval Mode applies to the built-in Administrator account (FilterAdministratorToken)
filterAdministratorToken.desc: Backs "User Account Control: Admin Approval Mode for the built-in Administrator account". When false, the built-in Administrator runs every application with full administrative privilege. Null when the value is absent, in which case the Windows default of disabled applies.

localAccountTokenFilterPolicy.name: localAccountTokenFilterPolicy
localAccountTokenFilterPolicy.title: Whether remote connections by local administrators receive an elevated token (LocalAccountTokenFilterPolicy)
localAccountTokenFilterPolicy.desc: Controls UAC remote restrictions for local (SAM) accounts. False builds a filtered token, so a local administrator connecting over the network has no administrative rights. True builds an elevated token and disables the remote restrictions, which is the insecure setting. Domain accounts are not affected. Null when the value is absent, in which case the Windows default of a filtered token applies, so a check for the secure state is written `localAccountTokenFilterPolicy != true`.

promptOnSecureDesktop.name: promptOnSecureDesktop
promptOnSecureDesktop.title: Whether elevation prompts are shown on the secure desktop (PromptOnSecureDesktop)
promptOnSecureDesktop.desc: Backs "User Account Control: Switch to the secure desktop when prompting for elevation". When false, prompts appear on the interactive user's desktop. Null when the value is absent, in which case the Windows default of enabled applies.

validateAdminCodeSignatures.name: validateAdminCodeSignatures
validateAdminCodeSignatures.title: Whether only signed and validated executables are elevated (ValidateAdminCodeSignatures)
validateAdminCodeSignatures.desc: Backs "User Account Control: Only elevate executables that are signed and validated", which enforces certificate path validation on any interactive application that requests elevation. Null when the value is absent, in which case the Windows default of disabled applies.

windows.uac.title: Windows User Account Control (UAC) policy
windows.uac.desc: User Account Control settings that back the "User Account Control" security options, read from HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Policies\System, together with the LocalAccountTokenFilterPolicy value in the same key that governs UAC remote restrictions for local accounts. These control whether Admin Approval Mode is on, how administrators and standard users are prompted for elevation, whether prompts use the secure desktop, installer detection, UIAccess restrictions, file and registry virtualization, and whether remote connections by local administrators receive a filtered token. On/off settings are exposed as booleans, with any non-zero DWORD reading true, and the two prompt behaviors as integers. Values are nullable: an absent value resolves to null so it is distinguishable from an explicit false or 0, and each field names the Windows default that applies when it is absent. Checks on a setting whose secure state is the default should therefore accept null, for example `windows.uac.localAccountTokenFilterPolicy != true`.

windows.update.name: windows.update

available.name: available
available.title: Updates that are available but not yet installed
available.desc: Answered from the Windows Update Agent's last detection rather than a live scan, so it returns in seconds instead of the minutes an online search against Windows Update or WSUS can take. Check `config.lastDetectionSuccess` for how recent that detection is.

config.name: config
config.title: Windows Update Agent configuration and freshness

entry.name: entry
entry.title: Windows update record
entry.desc: Single update reported by the Windows Update Agent: the `kbId` (for example "KB5034441"), human-readable `title`, `classification` (such as "Security Updates", "Critical Updates", or "Definition Updates"), the support URL, and the `cveIds` it addresses. Installed updates carry the install `date` and `operation`; available updates carry the `severity` and whether they require a reboot. Filter `windows.update.available` on `severity` or `cveIds` to find outstanding security-relevant updates.

installed.name: installed
installed.title: Updates that have been installed (Windows Update Agent history)

policy.name: policy
policy.title: Windows Update for Business and Automatic Updates group policy configuration
policy.desc: Each policy value is nullable: a null value signals that the setting is not configured, distinguishing an absent policy from one explicitly set to 0.

windows.update.title: Windows Update Agent
windows.update.desc: How a Windows host receives updates and what it has applied or has pending. The `config` field surfaces Windows Update Agent configuration and freshness (the effective catalog source, WSUS settings, the last successful detection / download / install times, and whether a reboot is pending). `installed` lists the updates the agent has applied (the installed-KB history), and `available` lists updates the agent has found but not yet installed, answered from the cache of its last detection rather than a live scan. Configuration is read from the registry and works even on connections that cannot run commands; the installed and available collections fall back to the Windows Update Agent COM API when commands are available.

windows.update.config.name: windows.update.config

auOptions.name: auOptions
auOptions.title: Automatic update behavior
auOptions.desc: The HKLM\...\AU\AUOptions value: 1=keep my computer up to date disabled, 2=notify before download, 3=auto-download and notify of install, 4=auto-download and schedule install, 5=allow local admin to choose. 0 when not configured.

catalogSource.name: catalogSource
catalogSource.title: Effective update catalog source
catalogSource.desc: One of "windowsUpdate" (direct Microsoft Update), "wsus" (a configured WSUS server), "windowsUpdateForBusiness", "disabled" (the agent or automatic updates are turned off, through either AU\NoAutoUpdate or the legacy AUOptions encoding), or "unknown" (the relevant registry keys could not be read).

lastDetectionError.name: lastDetectionError
lastDetectionError.title: Last detection error code (e.g., "0x80244022"); empty when the last detection succeeded

lastDetectionSuccess.name: lastDetectionSuccess
lastDetectionSuccess.title: Time of the last successful update detection

lastDownloadSuccess.name: lastDownloadSuccess
lastDownloadSuccess.title: Time of the last successful update download

lastInstallSuccess.name: lastInstallSuccess
lastInstallSuccess.title: Time of the last successful update install

policyState.name: policyState
policyState.title: Whether Windows Update for Business is configured
policyState.desc: The IsWUfBConfigured flag under HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\WindowsUpdate\UpdatePolicy\PolicyState, 1 when the host takes its update policy from Windows Update for Business. Null when the key is absent, which is the state of a host that was never enrolled.

rebootPending.name: rebootPending
rebootPending.title: Whether a reboot is pending from a previous update

useWUServer.name: useWUServer
useWUServer.title: Whether the host is directed to use the WSUS server (HKLM\...\AU\UseWUServer)

wsusStatusServerUrl.name: wsusStatusServerUrl
wsusStatusServerUrl.title: Configured WSUS status reporting server URL (HKLM\...\WindowsUpdate\WUStatusServer)

windows.update.config.title: Windows Update Agent configuration and freshness
windows.update.config.desc: Where a Windows host gets its updates and whether the Windows Update Agent is healthy. `catalogSource` summarizes the effective source ("windowsUpdate", "wsus", "windowsUpdateForBusiness", "disabled", or "unknown"); `wsusServerUrl` / `useWUServer` reveal WSUS configuration; the `lastDetectionSuccess` / `lastDownloadSuccess` / `lastInstallSuccess` times expose how recently the agent refreshed its view; and `rebootPending` flags hosts waiting on a restart before update state can be trusted. Read from the Windows registry, so it is available even on connections that cannot run commands.

windows.update.entry.name: windows.update.entry

categories.name: categories
categories.title: Update categories reported by the Windows Update Agent

classification.name: classification
classification.title: Update classification
classification.desc: Microsoft's update category, such as "Security Updates", "Critical Updates", "Update Rollups", "Definition Updates", "Drivers", or "Feature Packs". Empty when the agent does not report a category.

cveIds.name: cveIds
cveIds.title: CVE identifiers addressed by this update

date.name: date
date.title: Date the update was installed (installed updates only)

kbId.name: kbId
kbId.title: Knowledge base article ID (e.g., "KB5034441"); empty for updates without a KB

operation.name: operation
operation.title: Operation that produced this history entry (e.g., "Installation", "Uninstallation")

rebootRequired.name: rebootRequired
rebootRequired.title: Whether installing the update requires a reboot

severity.name: severity
severity.title: Microsoft severity rating for security updates (e.g., "Critical", "Important", "Moderate", "Low")

supportUrl.name: supportUrl
supportUrl.title: Vendor support or knowledge base URL

updateId.name: updateId
updateId.title: Update identity (Windows Update Agent UpdateID GUID, or package name when read from the registry)

windows.update.entry.title: Windows update record
windows.update.entry.desc: Single update reported by the Windows Update Agent: the `kbId` (for example "KB5034441"), human-readable `title`, `classification` (such as "Security Updates", "Critical Updates", or "Definition Updates"), the support URL, and the `cveIds` it addresses. Installed updates carry the install `date` and `operation`; available updates carry the `severity` and whether they require a reboot. Filter `windows.update.available` on `severity` or `cveIds` to find outstanding security-relevant updates.

windows.update.policy.name: windows.update.policy

allowOptionalContent.name: allowOptionalContent
allowOptionalContent.title: Enable optional updates / optional content (WindowsUpdate\SetAllowOptionalContent); null when not configured

allowTemporaryEnterpriseFeatureControl.name: allowTemporaryEnterpriseFeatureControl
allowTemporaryEnterpriseFeatureControl.title: Whether temporary enterprise feature control is allowed (WindowsUpdate\AllowTemporaryEnterpriseFeatureControl); null when not configured

automaticUpdatesEnabled.name: automaticUpdatesEnabled
automaticUpdatesEnabled.title: Whether automatic updates are configured and enabled (AU\NoAutoUpdate is present and 0)

deferFeatureUpdates.name: deferFeatureUpdates
deferFeatureUpdates.title: Whether feature update deferral is enabled (WindowsUpdate\DeferFeatureUpdates); null when not configured

deferFeatureUpdatesPeriodInDays.name: deferFeatureUpdatesPeriodInDays
deferFeatureUpdatesPeriodInDays.title: Number of days feature updates are deferred (WindowsUpdate\DeferFeatureUpdatesPeriodInDays); null when not configured

deferQualityUpdates.name: deferQualityUpdates
deferQualityUpdates.title: Whether quality update deferral is enabled (WindowsUpdate\DeferQualityUpdates); null when not configured

deferQualityUpdatesPeriodInDays.name: deferQualityUpdatesPeriodInDays
deferQualityUpdatesPeriodInDays.title: Number of days quality updates are deferred (WindowsUpdate\DeferQualityUpdatesPeriodInDays); null when not configured

disablePauseUXAccess.name: disablePauseUXAccess
disablePauseUXAccess.title: Whether access to pause updates is removed (WindowsUpdate\SetDisablePauseUXAccess); null when not configured

managePreviewBuilds.name: managePreviewBuilds
managePreviewBuilds.title: Manage preview builds (WindowsUpdate\ManagePreviewBuildsPolicyValue)
managePreviewBuilds.desc: 0 = disable preview builds, 1 = enable, 2 = enable for next release; null when not configured.

noAutoRebootWithLoggedOnUsers.name: noAutoRebootWithLoggedOnUsers
noAutoRebootWithLoggedOnUsers.title: Whether scheduled installations do not auto-restart while users are logged on (AU\NoAutoRebootWithLoggedOnUsers); null when not configured

noAutoUpdate.name: noAutoUpdate
noAutoUpdate.title: Whether automatic updates are turned off (AU\NoAutoUpdate); null when not configured

scheduledInstallDay.name: scheduledInstallDay
scheduledInstallDay.title: Scheduled install day (AU\ScheduledInstallDay): 0 = every day, 1-7 = Sunday-Saturday; null when not configured

scheduledInstallTime.name: scheduledInstallTime
scheduledInstallTime.title: Scheduled install time as the hour of day (AU\ScheduledInstallTime), 0-23; null when not configured

windows.update.policy.title: Windows Update for Business and Automatic Updates group policy
windows.update.policy.desc: Managed Windows Update policy as configured through group policy (the "Windows Components > Windows Update" administrative templates). Every value is read directly from the registry under `HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\WindowsUpdate` and its `AU` subkey, so this resource works on any connection where the registry is readable, including filesystem scans. Integer fields mirror the underlying REG_DWORD policy values and are null when the corresponding policy is not configured, which lets checks tell "explicitly set to 0" apart from "left at the default".

windows.winrm.name: windows.winrm

client.name: client
client.title: WinRM client authentication and transport policy

listener.name: listener
listener.title: WinRM listener
listener.desc: Single WS-Management listener: the transport it accepts, the address and port it is bound to, whether it is enabled, and, for an HTTPS listener, the hostname and certificate it presents. An HTTP listener carries session payloads without transport encryption unless the authentication mechanism encrypts them itself, so an internet-reachable HTTP listener combined with `windows.winrm.service.allowUnencryptedTraffic` is the pair worth auditing.

listeners.name: listeners
listeners.title: Configured WinRM listeners
listeners.desc: Every listener the WS-Management service is configured with, with the transport it accepts, the port and address it is bound to, and the certificate an HTTPS listener presents. A host with no listener configured reports an empty list, which is not the same as a failed read: a configuration that cannot be read (the WinRM service is stopped, or the connection cannot run commands) is an error, so an audit of the form "no listener accepts unencrypted HTTP" cannot pass by reading nothing.

service.name: service
service.title: WinRM service authentication, transport, and listener policy

serviceStartMode.name: serviceStartMode
serviceStartMode.title: WinRM service start mode (Services\WinRM\Start)
serviceStartMode.desc: The HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Services\WinRM\Start DWORD: 2=automatic, 3=manual, 4=disabled. Defaults to 3 (manual) when the value is absent.

windows.winrm.title: Windows Remote Management (WinRM)
windows.winrm.desc: Effective WinRM (Windows Remote Management) policy posture for both the WinRM client and service, plus the WinRS remote shell setting and the WinRM service start mode. The client and service settings are read from the Group Policy key HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\WinRM; these are GPO-only values with no per-listener effective fallback, so when a value is absent the documented Windows default applies. `serviceStartMode` reflects HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Services\WinRM\Start. Those fields are read from the registry, so they are available even on connections that cannot run commands. `listeners`, `client.trustedHosts`, `service.ipv4Filter` and `service.ipv6Filter` report the live WS-Management configuration instead and need a connection that can run commands.

windows.winrm.client.name: windows.winrm.client

allowBasic.name: allowBasic
allowBasic.title: Whether the WinRM client allows Basic authentication
allowBasic.desc: Reports the live WS-Management value (Client\Auth\Basic), which already reflects any Group Policy setting. True on a stock Windows Server: the client will offer Basic credentials when a server asks for them.

allowDigest.name: allowDigest
allowDigest.title: Whether the WinRM client allows Digest authentication
allowDigest.desc: Reports the live WS-Management value (Client\Auth\Digest), which already reflects any Group Policy setting. True on a stock Windows Server.

allowUnencryptedTraffic.name: allowUnencryptedTraffic
allowUnencryptedTraffic.title: Whether the WinRM client allows unencrypted traffic
allowUnencryptedTraffic.desc: Reports the live WS-Management value (Client\AllowUnencrypted), which already reflects any Group Policy setting. False on a stock Windows Server, so the client refuses to send an unencrypted request.

trustedHosts.name: trustedHosts
trustedHosts.title: Hosts the WinRM client trusts without mutual authentication (Client\TrustedHosts)
trustedHosts.desc: A comma-separated list, empty when no host is trusted. A single "*" trusts every host, which turns off the server authentication that otherwise stops the client from sending credentials to an impostor. Entries may also be wildcards such as "*.example.com" or the literal "<local>". Reports the live WS-Management value, which already reflects any Group Policy setting, so it needs a connection that can run commands.

windows.winrm.client.title: WinRM client policy
windows.winrm.client.desc: Live WS-Management client configuration, which already reflects any Group Policy setting applied to it. Reading these needs a connection that can run commands.

windows.winrm.listener.name: windows.winrm.listener

address.name: address
address.title: Address the listener is bound to
address.desc: Either "*" for every address, "IP:<address>" for a single address, or "MAC:<address>" for the addresses of one adapter.

certificateThumbprint.name: certificateThumbprint
certificateThumbprint.title: Thumbprint of the certificate an HTTPS listener presents, empty for HTTP

enabled.name: enabled
enabled.title: Whether the listener is enabled

hostname.name: hostname
hostname.title: Hostname the listener answers for, empty when it is not restricted
hostname.desc: For an HTTPS listener this is the name the presented certificate must match.

port.name: port
port.title: TCP port the listener is bound to, 0 when the port cannot be read
port.desc: The Windows defaults are 5985 for HTTP and 5986 for HTTPS. Older hosts configured before Windows Vista may still use 80 and 443.

transport.name: transport
transport.title: Transport the listener accepts, either HTTP or HTTPS

windows.winrm.listener.title: WinRM listener
windows.winrm.listener.desc: Single WS-Management listener: the transport it accepts, the address and port it is bound to, whether it is enabled, and, for an HTTPS listener, the hostname and certificate it presents. An HTTP listener carries session payloads without transport encryption unless the authentication mechanism encrypts them itself, so an internet-reachable HTTP listener combined with `windows.winrm.service.allowUnencryptedTraffic` is the pair worth auditing.

windows.winrm.service.name: windows.winrm.service

allowAutoConfig.name: allowAutoConfig
allowAutoConfig.title: Whether the WinRM service allows remote server management / auto config (Service\AllowAutoConfig)
allowAutoConfig.desc: Read from the policy key. Defaults to false (the listener is not auto-configured when the policy is not configured).

allowBasic.name: allowBasic
allowBasic.title: Whether the WinRM service accepts Basic authentication
allowBasic.desc: Reports the live WS-Management value (Service\Auth\Basic), which already reflects any Group Policy setting. False on a stock Windows Server. Basic authentication sends the password in a reversible encoding, so a service that accepts it over an unencrypted transport is handing out credentials.

allowRemoteShellAccess.name: allowRemoteShellAccess
allowRemoteShellAccess.title: Whether WinRS allows remote shell access
allowRemoteShellAccess.desc: Reports the live WS-Management value (Shell\AllowRemoteShellAccess), which already reflects any Group Policy setting. True on a stock Windows Server.

allowUnencryptedTraffic.name: allowUnencryptedTraffic
allowUnencryptedTraffic.title: Whether the WinRM service accepts unencrypted traffic
allowUnencryptedTraffic.desc: Reports the live WS-Management value (Service\AllowUnencrypted), which already reflects any Group Policy setting. False on a stock Windows Server. Together with allowBasic this is the pair worth auditing: an unencrypted transport is what turns Basic authentication into a credential disclosure.

disableRunAs.name: disableRunAs
disableRunAs.title: Whether the WinRM service disallows storing RunAs credentials (Service\DisableRunAs)
disableRunAs.desc: Read from the policy key. Defaults to false (RunAs credential storage is not disabled when the policy is not configured).

ipv4Filter.name: ipv4Filter
ipv4Filter.title: IPv4 addresses the WinRM service accepts requests on (Service\IPv4Filter)
ipv4Filter.desc: A comma-separated list of addresses or ranges, "*" for every IPv4 address, and empty when the service accepts no IPv4 request at all. Reports the live WS-Management value, which already reflects any Group Policy setting, so it needs a connection that can run commands.

ipv6Filter.name: ipv6Filter
ipv6Filter.title: IPv6 addresses the WinRM service accepts requests on (Service\IPv6Filter)
ipv6Filter.desc: A comma-separated list of addresses or ranges, "*" for every IPv6 address, and empty when the service accepts no IPv6 request at all. Reports the live WS-Management value, which already reflects any Group Policy setting, so it needs a connection that can run commands.

windows.winrm.service.title: WinRM service policy
windows.winrm.service.desc: The WinRM service configuration. The authentication, encryption and remote shell settings are read live from WS-Management, which already reflects any Group Policy applied to them, so reading those needs a connection that can run commands. The remaining settings exist only under HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\WinRM\Service and fall back to the documented Windows default when no policy sets them.

windsurf.name: windsurf

configPath.name: configPath
configPath.title: Path to the Windsurf configuration directory

mcpServer.name: mcpServer
mcpServer.title: Windsurf MCP server configuration
mcpServer.desc: Model Context Protocol server Windsurf is configured to use. Stdio servers launch a local command with args; sse servers connect to a url. `type` reports the transport and hasEnv whether environment variables (often holding API keys or tokens) are configured for the server.

mcpServers.name: mcpServers
mcpServers.title: MCP servers the editor connects to

package.name: package
package.title: Package that installed this tool
package.desc: Resolves to the system-package-manager entry that installed the tool when one can be identified; otherwise an abstract package (origin "unknown", empty format, absent from `packages`) that records the tool's presence and, where determinable, an inferred version. Read `.installed` for the install signal, or any package field (`version`, `purl`, `vendor`) for detail.

repo.name: repo
repo.title: Windsurf workspace repository
repo.desc: Git repository backing a workspace folder opened in Windsurf, derived from the editor's opened-folder history and resolved through its `.git/config`. Exposes the origin remote `url`, the parsed `host` (for example github.com) and `name` (org/repo slug), the checked-out `branch`, all configured `remotes`, and the working-tree root `path`. Repositories are deduplicated by their working-tree root. Opened folders that are not git working trees are omitted.

repos.name: repos
repos.title: Git repositories backing the opened workspaces

rule.name: rule
rule.title: Windsurf rule / memory file
rule.desc: Rule or memory file that injects standing instructions into the Windsurf assistant's context. The content field holds the full text, which shapes how the AI behaves and is worth reviewing for injected or unexpected directives.

rules.name: rules
rules.title: Global rules and memories that steer the assistant

runtime.name: runtime
runtime.title: Host the agent runs in
runtime.desc: The environment the agent runs inside: the operating system for a standalone agent, the IDE/editor for an editor plugin, or the browser for a browser extension. The runtime's `package` carries the host's software identity (version and purl where known) so its own version and vulnerabilities can be looked up like any other software. Optional, null when the host cannot be determined.

skill.name: skill
skill.title: Windsurf skill
skill.desc: Skill defined by a SKILL.md file that packages task instructions for the assistant. The allowedTools list bounds which tools the skill may invoke, argumentHint documents its expected arguments, and content holds the full definition. Use sha256 to detect tampering.

skills.name: skills
skills.title: Installed skills

windsurf.title: Windsurf editor (Codeium) instance
windsurf.desc: Windsurf AI code editor from Codeium installed on the host. Queryable through it are the global rules and memories that steer the assistant, the configured MCP servers, and any installed skills, along with the package that installed the editor and the runtime it executes in. URL: https://windsurf.com/

type.name: type

url.name: url
url.title: Endpoint URL for sse or streamable-http servers

remotes.name: remotes

url.name: url
url.title: Origin remote URL

Exposes the origin remote `url`, the parsed `host` (for example github.com) and `name` (org/repo slug), the checked-out `branch`, all configured `remotes`, and the working-tree root `path`. windsurf.skill.name: windsurf.skill

allowedTools.name: allowedTools

argumentHint.name: argumentHint

content.name: content

sha256.name: sha256

winget.name: winget

architecture.name: architecture
architecture.title: Processor architecture of the App Installer package, for example x64 or arm64

enabledByPolicy.name: enabledByPolicy
enabledByPolicy.title: Whether Group Policy allows winget to run
enabledByPolicy.desc: False when the EnableAppInstaller or EnableWindowsPackageManagerCommandLineInterfaces policy is set to disabled.

installed.name: installed
installed.title: Whether a winget.exe the machine can run is present

missingDependencies.name: missingDependencies
missingDependencies.title: Framework packages App Installer requires that are not present
missingDependencies.desc: Each entry names a PackageDependency from the package manifest that no package on the machine satisfies with the same architecture (or neutral) and at least the required version, as `<name> >= <minVersion>`. Null when winget is not installed or its manifest cannot be read.

packageFullName.name: packageFullName
packageFullName.title: Full name of the App Installer package

path.name: path
path.title: Path to winget.exe, null when winget is not installed

source.name: source
source.title: winget package source

sources.name: sources
sources.title: Package sources winget uses for the SYSTEM account
sources.desc: The defaults (msstore, winget, winget-font) unless Group Policy disables them, sources added by Group Policy, and sources added or removed for the SYSTEM account, filtered by the allowed-sources policy.

systemUsable.name: systemUsable
systemUsable.title: Whether winget can run as the SYSTEM account
systemUsable.desc: True when winget.exe is present for an architecture the machine runs, every framework package the manifest requires is present, and Group Policy does not disable winget. False whenever Group Policy disables winget. Otherwise null when the package manifest cannot be read. This is a read-only check: winget is not started.

version.name: version
version.title: Version of winget.exe
version.desc: The product version of winget.exe, which is what `winget --version` reports, for example 1.29.380.0. It can be higher than the App Installer package version in packageFullName. When the file version cannot be read, the package version is reported. Null when winget is not installed.

winget.title: Windows Package Manager (winget)
winget.desc: Whether winget is installed on a Windows host and whether it can run as the SYSTEM account, where it often cannot. installed, version, and path come from the Microsoft.DesktopAppInstaller package that ships winget.exe, found in the AppX package repository and the WindowsApps folder without running winget. missingDependencies lists the framework packages its manifest requires that the machine does not have, and systemUsable combines these checks, for example `winget.installed && winget.systemUsable`. sources lists the package sources winget uses for the SYSTEM account. On any other platform installed and systemUsable are false.

explicit.name: explicit
explicit.title: Whether the source is only used when named explicitly

name.name: name
name.title: Source name, for example winget or msstore

origin.name: origin
origin.title: Where the source is defined: default, policy, or user

type.name: type
type.title: Source type, for example Microsoft.PreIndexed.Package or Microsoft.Rest

package.name: package
package.title: WordPress plugin
package.desc: Single installed WordPress plugin, exposing its slug, display name, version, license, and the minimum required and maximum tested WordPress versions declared in its header.

packages.name: packages
packages.title: WordPress plugin inventory
packages.desc: WordPress plugins installed under wp-content/plugins/, each with its version and supported WordPress version range. Useful for spotting plugins that are untested against the running WordPress version. Set `path` to the plugins directory.

wordpress.package.name: wordpress.package

files.name: files
files.title: Files that contributed this plugin to the inventory

purl.name: purl
purl.title: Package URL (purl), a standardized identifier for the plugin

version.name: version

wordpress.package.title: WordPress plugin
wordpress.package.desc: Single installed WordPress plugin, exposing its slug, display name, version, license, and the minimum required and maximum tested WordPress versions declared in its header.

wordpress.packages.name: wordpress.packages

files.name: files
files.title: Files used to determine the packages

wordpress.packages.title: WordPress plugin inventory
wordpress.packages.desc: WordPress plugins installed under wp-content/plugins/, each with its version and supported WordPress version range. Useful for spotting plugins that are untested against the running WordPress version. Set `path` to the plugins directory.

yum.name: yum

config.name: config
config.title: Yum/DNF global configuration
config.desc: System-wide package manager configuration: the `[main]` section of `/etc/yum.conf`, or `/etc/dnf/dnf.conf` on dnf-based systems. Use `gpgcheck` and `localPkgGpgcheck` to assert that package signature verification is enforced for every repository and for locally installed packages, a core CIS supply-chain control; `repoGpgcheck` extends that to repository metadata. The bool accessors report the value the package manager uses: the directive in the file, on dnf 5 applied over the drop-in files in `/usr/share/dnf5/libdnf.conf.d` and `/etc/dnf/libdnf5.conf.d` (on dnf 5 `gpgcheck` reads `pkg_gpgcheck`, the option it is another name for), and the package manager's default when no file sets it. `params` exposes every `[main]` directive of the file as a raw string map for settings without a dedicated accessor. Select an alternate file with `yum.config(path: "...")`; drop-in files do not apply to it. Where the file does not exist and no yum or dnf is installed, or a file named with `path` does not exist, `content`, `params` and the bool fields are null.

repo.name: repo
repo.title: Yum repository
repo.desc: A single configured yum/dnf repository as reported by `yum -v repolist all`, or `dnf5 repo info --all` on dnf 5 hosts such as Fedora 41+ and Amazon Linux 2027: its `id`, human-readable `name`, `status`, `baseurl` list, expiry indicator, backing configuration `file`, `revision`, package count, size, mirror list, and whether it is currently `enabled`. Select a repository by ID, for example `yum.repo(id: "baseos")`.

repos.name: repos
repos.title: List of all configured Yum repositories

vars.name: vars
vars.title: Variables available for substitution in yum/dnf repository configuration
vars.desc: The built-in `arch`, `basearch`, and `releasever` as dnf computes them, plus the custom variables defined on disk: one file per variable in `/etc/yum/vars` and `/etc/dnf/vars` (dnf 4), or `/usr/share/dnf5/vars.d` and `/etc/dnf/vars` (dnf 5), named after the file with the file's first line as the value. A variable in `/etc/dnf/vars` overrides one of the same name in the other directory, and a custom variable overrides a built-in one, the same way dnf resolves them. The built-in variables come from dnf's Python API, yum's on RHEL 7 and older, or `dnf5 --dump-variables`, and are missing where none of these can run, such as image scans.

yum.title: Yum/DNF package manager
yum.desc: Configuration of the yum/dnf package manager on RedHat-family systems. `vars` exposes the variables defined across `/etc/yum.conf` and the `.repo` files (for example `$releasever` and `$basearch`) and `repos` lists every configured repository as `yum.repo` entries.

yum.config.title: Yum/DNF global configuration
yum.config.desc: System-wide package manager configuration: the `[main]` section of `/etc/yum.conf`, or `/etc/dnf/dnf.conf` on dnf-based systems. Use `gpgcheck` and `localPkgGpgcheck` to assert that package signature verification is enforced for every repository and for locally installed packages, a core CIS supply-chain control; `repoGpgcheck` extends that to repository metadata. The bool accessors report the value the package manager uses: the directive in the file, on dnf 5 applied over the drop-in files in `/usr/share/dnf5/libdnf.conf.d` and `/etc/dnf/libdnf5.conf.d` (on dnf 5 `gpgcheck` reads `pkg_gpgcheck`, the option it is another name for), and the package manager's default when no file sets it. `params` exposes every `[main]` directive of the file as a raw string map for settings without a dedicated accessor. Select an alternate file with `yum.config(path: "...")`; drop-in files do not apply to it. Where the file does not exist and no yum or dnf is installed, or a file named with `path` does not exist, `content`, `params` and the bool fields are null.

pkgs.name: pkgs

yum.repo.title: Yum repository
yum.repo.desc: A single configured yum/dnf repository as reported by `yum -v repolist all`, or `dnf5 repo info --all` on dnf 5 hosts such as Fedora 41+ and Amazon Linux 2027: its `id`, human-readable `name`, `status`, `baseurl` list, expiry indicator, backing configuration `file`, `revision`, package count, size, mirror list, and whether it is currently `enabled`. Select a repository by ID, for example `yum.repo(id: "baseos")`.

zed.name: zed

configPath.name: configPath
configPath.title: Path to the Zed configuration directory

model.name: model
model.title: Configured default model
model.desc: The model Zed's agent is configured to use by default, taken from `agent.default_model.model` in settings.json (for example "claude-sonnet-4"). Empty when no default agent model is set.

modelProvider.name: modelProvider
modelProvider.title: Configured model provider
modelProvider.desc: The backend that serves the default agent model, taken from `agent.default_model.provider` in settings.json (for example "anthropic" or "zed.dev"). Empty when unset.

package.name: package
package.title: Package that installed this tool
package.desc: Resolves to the system-package-manager entry that installed the tool when one can be identified; otherwise an abstract package (origin "unknown", empty format, absent from `packages`) that records the tool's presence and, where determinable, an inferred version. Read `.installed` for the install signal, or any package field (`version`, `purl`, `vendor`) for detail.

repo.name: repo
repo.title: Zed workspace repository
repo.desc: Git repository backing a workspace opened in Zed, derived from the paths recorded in Zed's workspace database and resolved through their `.git/config`. Exposes the origin remote `url`, the parsed `host` (for example github.com) and `name` (org/repo slug), the checked-out `branch`, all configured `remotes`, and the working-tree root `path`. Repositories are deduplicated by their working-tree root. Workspace paths that are not git working trees are omitted.

repos.name: repos
repos.title: Git repositories backing the opened workspaces

runtime.name: runtime
runtime.title: Host the agent runs in
runtime.desc: The environment the agent runs inside: the operating system for a standalone agent, the IDE/editor for an editor plugin, or the browser for a browser extension. The runtime's `package` carries the host's software identity (version and purl where known) so its own version and vulnerabilities can be looked up like any other software. Optional, null when the host cannot be determined.

settings.name: settings
settings.title: Full settings dictionary parsed from the Zed configuration

zed.title: Zed editor instance
zed.desc: Zed code editor installed on the host. Queryable through it are the workspace settings dictionary and the names of installed extensions, along with the package that installed the editor and the runtime it executes in. URL: https://zed.dev/

zed.repo.name: zed.repo

branch.name: branch
branch.title: Currently checked-out branch
branch.desc: The branch referenced by HEAD, for example main. Empty when HEAD is detached or cannot be read.

host.name: host
host.title: Remote host parsed from the origin URL
host.desc: For example github.com or gitlab.com. Empty when there is no remote or the URL cannot be parsed.

name.name: name
name.title: Repository slug parsed from the origin URL
name.desc: The owner-and-name path, for example mondoohq/mql. Empty when there is no remote or the URL cannot be parsed.

remotes.name: remotes
remotes.title: All configured remotes, keyed by remote name

url.name: url
url.title: Origin remote URL
url.desc: The fetch URL of the remote named origin, or the first remote found when there is no origin. Empty for a repository with no remotes.

zfs.name: zfs

dataset.name: dataset
dataset.title: ZFS dataset (filesystem, volume, snapshot, or bookmark)
dataset.desc: Single ZFS dataset: full `name`, `type` (filesystem, volume, snapshot, bookmark), used/available/referenced bytes, `mountpoint`, compression algorithm and ratio, `mounted` flag, record size, quota, reservation, `origin` snapshot for clones, creation time, encryption algorithm, full `properties` map, and `snapshots` list. Initialize by name or iterate from `zfs.datasets`.

datasets.name: datasets
datasets.title: All ZFS datasets (filesystems, volumes, snapshots, bookmarks)

pool.name: pool
pool.title: ZFS storage pool
pool.desc: Single ZFS storage pool: `name`, `guid`, health status, total/allocated/free bytes, fragmentation percentage, space utilization, deduplication ratio, read-only flag, auto-expand/replace/trim settings, the top-level `vdevs` topology, and the full `properties` map. Initialize by name (e.g., `zfs.pool(name: "tank")`) or iterate from `zfs.pools`.

version.name: version
version.title: ZFS version string
version.desc: The OpenZFS release, for example `zfs-2.2.2-1`. ZFS on Linux before 0.8 reports the release of its loaded kernel module, for example `zfs-kmod-0.6.5.6-0ubuntu28`. Oracle Solaris names its ZFS release by the pool version instead, for example `53`.

zfs.title: ZFS storage pools and datasets
zfs.desc: ZFS storage on the host: the installed `version`, the storage `pools` with their health and capacity, and every `dataset` (filesystems, volumes, snapshots, and bookmarks). Iterate to audit pool health, free capacity, vdev topology, and dataset properties such as compression and encryption.

vdev.name: vdev
vdev.title: ZFS virtual device (vdev) in a pool's topology
vdev.desc: Single vdev within a pool: its `name` (e.g., "raidz2-0", "mirror-0"), `type`, `state`, device `path` (for leaf vdevs), read/write/checksum error counts, slow I/O count, number of child devices, and the nested `devices` list.
